module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.ProjectionValuedMeasure.Basic
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Complex
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.Variation.Basic

/-!
# Scalar coefficient measures of projection-valued measures

For a projection-valued measure `E` and vectors `g h`, the scalar coefficient
measure is

`E.scalarMeasure g h s = ⟪h, E s g⟫_ℂ`.

Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in the first argument.  Thus the
measure is complex-linear in `g` and conjugate-linear in `h`.  Its total
variation satisfies the sharp local estimate

`|E_{g,h}|(s) ≤ ‖E(s)g‖ ‖h‖`

for measurable `s`, and hence the global estimate
`|E_{g,h}|(univ) ≤ ‖g‖ ‖h‖`.

This is the coefficient measure and total-variation estimate in Conway,
*A Course in Functional Analysis*, second edition, Chapter IX, Lemma 1.9.
-/

@[expose] public section

open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped ENNReal InnerProductSpace NNReal

namespace MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace
namespace ProjectionValuedMeasure

noncomputable section

universe u v

variable {X : Type u} {H : Type v}
variable [MeasurableSpace X]
variable [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]

/-- The complex measure `s ↦ ⟪h, E(s)g⟫`. -/
noncomputable def scalarMeasure (E : ProjectionValuedMeasure X H) (g h : H) :
    ComplexMeasure X :=
  VectorMeasure.mapRangeL (innerSL ℂ h) (E.applyVectorMeasure g)

@[simp]
theorem scalarMeasure_apply (E : ProjectionValuedMeasure X H) (g h : H) (s : Set X) :
    E.scalarMeasure g h s = ⟪h, E s g⟫_ℂ := by
  change (innerSL ℂ h) (E.applyVectorMeasure g s) = ⟪h, E s g⟫_ℂ
  rfl

theorem scalarMeasure_add_left (E : ProjectionValuedMeasure X H) (g₁ g₂ h : H) :
    E.scalarMeasure (g₁ + g₂) h = E.scalarMeasure g₁ h + E.scalarMeasure g₂ h := by
  apply VectorMeasure.ext
  intro s hs
  simp [scalarMeasure_apply, map_add, inner_add_right]

theorem scalarMeasure_smul_left (E : ProjectionValuedMeasure X H) (c : ℂ) (g h : H) :
    E.scalarMeasure (c • g) h = c • E.scalarMeasure g h := by
  apply VectorMeasure.ext
  intro s hs
  simp [scalarMeasure_apply, map_smul, inner_smul_right]

theorem scalarMeasure_add_right (E : ProjectionValuedMeasure X H) (g h₁ h₂ : H) :
    E.scalarMeasure g (h₁ + h₂) = E.scalarMeasure g h₁ + E.scalarMeasure g h₂ := by
  apply VectorMeasure.ext
  intro s hs
  simp [scalarMeasure_apply, inner_add_left]

theorem scalarMeasure_smul_right (E : ProjectionValuedMeasure X H) (c : ℂ) (g h : H) :
    E.scalarMeasure g (c • h) = star c • E.scalarMeasure g h := by
  apply VectorMeasure.ext
  intro s hs
  simp [scalarMeasure_apply, inner_smul_left]

omit [CompleteSpace H] in
private theorem norm_finsetSum_sq_eq
    {ι : Type*} (u : Finset ι) (v : ι → H)
    (hv : ∀ i ∈ u, ∀ j ∈ u, i ≠ j → ⟪v i, v j⟫_ℂ = 0) :
    ‖∑ i ∈ u, v i‖ * ‖∑ i ∈ u, v i‖ =
      ∑ i ∈ u, ‖v i‖ * ‖v i‖ := by
  classical
  induction u using Finset.induction_on with
  | empty => simp
  | @insert a u ha ih =>
      have haorth : ⟪v a, ∑ i ∈ u, v i⟫_ℂ = 0 := by
        rw [inner_sum]
        apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
        intro i hi
        exact hv a (Finset.mem_insert_self _ _) i (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hi)
          (fun hai ↦ ha (hai ▸ hi))
      rw [Finset.sum_insert ha,
        norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_of_inner_eq_zero _ _ haorth,
        ih (fun i hi j hj hij ↦ hv i (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hi)
          j (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hj) hij),
        Finset.sum_insert ha]

private theorem sum_norm_scalarMeasure_le
    (E : ProjectionValuedMeasure X H) (g h : H) {s : Set X} (hs : MeasurableSet s)
    (P : Finset (Set X)) (hPsub : ∀ t ∈ P, t ⊆ s)
    (hPdisj : (P : Set (Set X)).PairwiseDisjoint id)
    (hPmeas : ∀ t ∈ P, MeasurableSet t) :
    ∑ t ∈ P, ‖E.scalarMeasure g h t‖ ≤ ‖E s g‖ * ‖h‖ := by
  classical
  let μ : ComplexMeasure X := E.scalarMeasure g h
  choose c hc_norm hc_phase using fun t : Set X ↦ Complex.exists_norm_eq_mul_self (μ t)
  let v : Set X → H := fun t ↦ c t • E t g
  have horthE : ∀ i ∈ P, ∀ j ∈ P, i ≠ j → ⟪E i g, E j g⟫_ℂ = 0 := by
    intro i hi j hj hij
    exact E.inner_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint (hPmeas i hi) (hPmeas j hj)
      (hPdisj hi hj hij) g g
  have horthv : ∀ i ∈ P, ∀ j ∈ P, i ≠ j → ⟪v i, v j⟫_ℂ = 0 := by
    intro i hi j hj hij
    simp only [v, inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right, horthE i hi j hj hij,
      mul_zero, starRingEnd_apply]
  have hnormsum : ‖∑ t ∈ P, v t‖ = ‖∑ t ∈ P, E t g‖ := by
    apply (sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).mp
    simp only [pow_two]
    rw [norm_finsetSum_sq_eq P v horthv,
      norm_finsetSum_sq_eq P (fun t ↦ E t g) horthE]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro t ht
    rw [norm_smul, hc_norm t, one_mul]
  let U : Set X := ⋃ t ∈ P, t
  have hUmeas : MeasurableSet U := by
    dsimp only [U]
    exact MeasurableSet.biUnion (Finset.countable_toSet P) (by simpa using hPmeas)
  have hUsub : U ⊆ s := by
    dsimp only [U]
    exact iUnion₂_subset fun t ht ↦ hPsub t ht
  have hsumE : ∑ t ∈ P, E t g = E U g := by
    have hsumOp := E.biUnion_finset P id hPmeas hPdisj
    have happ := congrArg (fun T : H →L[ℂ] H ↦ T g) hsumOp
    simpa only [U, sum_apply, id_eq] using happ.symm
  have hproj : E U g = E U (E s g) := by
    have hinter := E.inter U hUmeas s hs
    rw [Set.inter_eq_left.mpr hUsub] at hinter
    calc
      E U g = (E U * E s) g := congrArg (fun T : H →L[ℂ] H ↦ T g) hinter
      _ = E U (E s g) := rfl
  have hsumE_le : ‖∑ t ∈ P, E t g‖ ≤ ‖E s g‖ := by
    rw [hsumE, hproj]
    calc
      ‖E U (E s g)‖ ≤ ‖E U‖ * ‖E s g‖ := E U |>.le_opNorm _
      _ ≤ 1 * ‖E s g‖ := by
        gcongr
        exact IsStarProjection.norm_le _ (E.isStarProjection U)
      _ = ‖E s g‖ := one_mul _
  have hphase : ((∑ t ∈ P, ‖μ t‖ : ℝ) : ℂ) = ⟪h, ∑ t ∈ P, v t⟫_ℂ := by
    rw [inner_sum]
    push_cast
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro t ht
    rw [show ⟪h, v t⟫_ℂ = c t * μ t by
      simp only [v, inner_smul_right, μ, scalarMeasure_apply]]
    exact hc_phase t
  calc
    ∑ t ∈ P, ‖E.scalarMeasure g h t‖ = ‖((∑ t ∈ P, ‖μ t‖ : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ := by
      rw [Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs,
        abs_of_nonneg (Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ ↦ norm_nonneg _)]
    _ = ‖⟪h, ∑ t ∈ P, v t⟫_ℂ‖ := congrArg norm hphase
    _ ≤ ‖h‖ * ‖∑ t ∈ P, v t‖ := norm_inner_le_norm _ _
    _ = ‖h‖ * ‖∑ t ∈ P, E t g‖ := by rw [hnormsum]
    _ ≤ ‖h‖ * ‖E s g‖ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hsumE_le (norm_nonneg _)
    _ = ‖E s g‖ * ‖h‖ := mul_comm _ _

/-- Sharp local total-variation bound for a scalar coefficient measure. -/
theorem scalarMeasure_variation_le (E : ProjectionValuedMeasure X H) (g h : H)
    {s : Set X} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    (E.scalarMeasure g h).variation s ≤
      (((‖E s g‖₊ * ‖h‖₊ : ℝ≥0) : ℝ≥0∞)) := by
  let μ : ComplexMeasure X := E.scalarMeasure g h
  let C : ℝ≥0∞ := ((‖E s g‖₊ * ‖h‖₊ : ℝ≥0) : ℝ≥0∞)
  by_contra hle
  have hlt : C < μ.variation s := lt_of_not_ge hle
  obtain ⟨P, hPsub, hPdisj, hPmeas, hPsum⟩ :=
    VectorMeasure.exists_lt_sum_of_lt_variation μ hs hlt
  have hreal := sum_norm_scalarMeasure_le E g h hs P hPsub hPdisj hPmeas
  have hnnreal : ∑ t ∈ P, ‖μ t‖₊ ≤ ‖E s g‖₊ * ‖h‖₊ := by
    apply NNReal.coe_le_coe.mp
    simpa only [NNReal.coe_sum, coe_nnnorm, NNReal.coe_mul] using hreal
  have hennreal : ∑ t ∈ P, ‖μ t‖ₑ ≤ C := by
    have hcoe := ENNReal.coe_le_coe.mpr hnnreal
    simpa only [enorm_eq_nnnorm, ENNReal.ofNNReal_finsetSum, C] using hcoe
  exact (not_lt_of_ge hennreal) hPsum

/-- Conway's global total-variation estimate
`|E_{g,h}|(X) ≤ ‖g‖ ‖h‖`. -/
theorem scalarMeasure_variation_univ_le (E : ProjectionValuedMeasure X H) (g h : H) :
    (E.scalarMeasure g h).variation Set.univ ≤
      (((‖g‖₊ * ‖h‖₊ : ℝ≥0) : ℝ≥0∞)) := by
  simpa only [E.univ, one_apply_eq_self] using
    E.scalarMeasure_variation_le g h MeasurableSet.univ

/-- Scalar coefficient measures have finite total variation. -/
noncomputable instance instIsFiniteMeasureVariationScalarMeasure
    (E : ProjectionValuedMeasure X H) (g h : H) :
    IsFiniteMeasure (E.scalarMeasure g h).variation where
  measure_univ_lt_top :=
    (E.scalarMeasure_variation_univ_le g h).trans_lt (by finiteness)

theorem scalarMeasure_variation_univ_lt_top
    (E : ProjectionValuedMeasure X H) (g h : H) :
    (E.scalarMeasure g h).variation Set.univ < ∞ := by
  finiteness

/-- Real-valued form of the sharp local variation estimate. -/
theorem scalarMeasure_variation_real_le (E : ProjectionValuedMeasure X H) (g h : H)
    {s : Set X} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    (E.scalarMeasure g h).variation.real s ≤ ‖E s g‖ * ‖h‖ := by
  rw [measureReal_def]
  calc
    ((E.scalarMeasure g h).variation s).toReal ≤
        ((((‖E s g‖₊ * ‖h‖₊ : ℝ≥0) : ℝ≥0∞))).toReal :=
      ENNReal.toReal_mono (by finiteness) (E.scalarMeasure_variation_le g h hs)
    _ = ‖E s g‖ * ‖h‖ := by simp

/-- Real-valued global variation estimate. -/
theorem scalarMeasure_variation_real_univ_le
    (E : ProjectionValuedMeasure X H) (g h : H) :
    (E.scalarMeasure g h).variation.real Set.univ ≤ ‖g‖ * ‖h‖ := by
  simpa only [E.univ, one_apply_eq_self] using
    E.scalarMeasure_variation_real_le g h MeasurableSet.univ

end

end ProjectionValuedMeasure
end MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace

Author: @toskua

module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Representation.SupportCompression
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Compact.Basic

/-!
# Rectangular operators between represented unit ranges

A possibly nonunital representation of a unital algebra has an actual unit
range. This file constructs the rectangular operator between two such ranges
and proves that an original compact intertwining defect remains compact.
No Fredholmness or global-index agreement is asserted by this construction.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace NonUnitalStarAlgHom

universe uA uH₀ uH₁

variable {A : Type uA} [Semiring A] [Algebra ℂ A] [StarRing A]
variable {H₀ : Type uH₀} [NormedAddCommGroup H₀] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H₀]
  [CompleteSpace H₀]
variable {H₁ : Type uH₁} [NormedAddCommGroup H₁] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H₁]
  [CompleteSpace H₁]

/-- Compress an actual rectangular operator to the two represented unit
ranges, using the target unit image and the original source inclusion. -/
noncomputable def unitRangeCompression
    (σ₀ : A →⋆ₙₐ[ℂ] (H₀ →L[ℂ] H₀))
    (σ₁ : A →⋆ₙₐ[ℂ] (H₁ →L[ℂ] H₁)) (T : H₀ →L[ℂ] H₁) :
    (σ₀ (1 : A)).range →L[ℂ] (σ₁ (1 : A)).range :=
  (σ₁ (1 : A)).rangeRestrict.comp (T.domRestrict ((σ₀ (1 : A)).range))

/-- The included supported value is the literal target unit image applied
to the original operator value. This permits zero or finite support. -/
@[simp]
theorem unitRangeCompression_apply
    (σ₀ : A →⋆ₙₐ[ℂ] (H₀ →L[ℂ] H₀))
    (σ₁ : A →⋆ₙₐ[ℂ] (H₁ →L[ℂ] H₁)) (T : H₀ →L[ℂ] H₁)
    (x : (σ₀ (1 : A)).range) :
    (unitRangeCompression σ₀ σ₁ T x : H₁) = σ₁ (1 : A) (T (x : H₀)) := rfl

/-- The supported intertwining defect factors through exactly the original
rectangular defect, followed by the actual target range map. -/
theorem unitRangeCompression_intertwining
    (σ₀ : A →⋆ₙₐ[ℂ] (H₀ →L[ℂ] H₀))
    (σ₁ : A →⋆ₙₐ[ℂ] (H₁ →L[ℂ] H₁)) (T : H₀ →L[ℂ] H₁) (a : A) :
    letI : CompleteSpace (σ₀ (1 : A)).range :=
      (ContinuousLinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.isClosed_range
        ((IsStarProjection.one A).map σ₀).isIdempotentElem).completeSpace_coe;
    letI : CompleteSpace (σ₁ (1 : A)).range :=
      (ContinuousLinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.isClosed_range
        ((IsStarProjection.one A).map σ₁).isIdempotentElem).completeSpace_coe;
    (unitRangeCompression σ₀ σ₁ T).comp (unitRangeStarAlgHom σ₀ a) -
        (unitRangeStarAlgHom σ₁ a).comp (unitRangeCompression σ₀ σ₁ T) =
      (σ₁ (1 : A)).rangeRestrict.comp
        ((T.comp (σ₀ a) - (σ₁ a).comp T).domRestrict ((σ₀ (1 : A)).range)) := by
  let : CompleteSpace (σ₀ (1 : A)).range :=
    (ContinuousLinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.isClosed_range
      ((IsStarProjection.one A).map σ₀).isIdempotentElem).completeSpace_coe
  let : CompleteSpace (σ₁ (1 : A)).range :=
    (ContinuousLinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.isClosed_range
      ((IsStarProjection.one A).map σ₁).isIdempotentElem).completeSpace_coe
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
  intro x
  apply Subtype.ext
  have hleft (y : H₁) : σ₁ (1 : A) (σ₁ a y) = σ₁ a y := by
    have h : σ₁ (1 : A) * σ₁ a = σ₁ a := by
      rw [← map_mul σ₁ (1 : A) a, one_mul]
    exact congrArg (fun V : H₁ →L[ℂ] H₁ => V y) h
  have hright (y : H₁) : σ₁ a (σ₁ (1 : A) y) = σ₁ a y := by
    have h : σ₁ a * σ₁ (1 : A) = σ₁ a := by
      rw [← map_mul σ₁ a (1 : A), mul_one]
    exact congrArg (fun V : H₁ →L[ℂ] H₁ => V y) h
  change
    (unitRangeCompression σ₀ σ₁ T (unitRangeStarAlgHom σ₀ a x) : H₁) -
        (unitRangeStarAlgHom σ₁ a (unitRangeCompression σ₀ σ₁ T x) : H₁) =
      σ₁ (1 : A) (T (σ₀ a (x : H₀)) - σ₁ a (T (x : H₀)))
  simp only [unitRangeCompression_apply, unitRangeStarAlgHom_apply,
    map_sub, hleft, hright]

/-- An original compact intertwining defect stays compact on the actual
unit supports. Compactness is derived by the displayed factorization. -/
theorem unitRangeCompression_intertwining_compact
    (σ₀ : A →⋆ₙₐ[ℂ] (H₀ →L[ℂ] H₀))
    (σ₁ : A →⋆ₙₐ[ℂ] (H₁ →L[ℂ] H₁)) (T : H₀ →L[ℂ] H₁) (a : A)
    (h : IsCompactOperator (T.comp (σ₀ a) - (σ₁ a).comp T)) :
    letI : CompleteSpace (σ₀ (1 : A)).range :=
      (ContinuousLinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.isClosed_range
        ((IsStarProjection.one A).map σ₀).isIdempotentElem).completeSpace_coe;
    letI : CompleteSpace (σ₁ (1 : A)).range :=
      (ContinuousLinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.isClosed_range
        ((IsStarProjection.one A).map σ₁).isIdempotentElem).completeSpace_coe;
    IsCompactOperator
      ((unitRangeCompression σ₀ σ₁ T).comp (unitRangeStarAlgHom σ₀ a) -
        (unitRangeStarAlgHom σ₁ a).comp (unitRangeCompression σ₀ σ₁ T)) := by
  let : CompleteSpace (σ₀ (1 : A)).range :=
    (ContinuousLinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.isClosed_range
      ((IsStarProjection.one A).map σ₀).isIdempotentElem).completeSpace_coe
  let : CompleteSpace (σ₁ (1 : A)).range :=
    (ContinuousLinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.isClosed_range
      ((IsStarProjection.one A).map σ₁).isIdempotentElem).completeSpace_coe
  rw [unitRangeCompression_intertwining]
  exact (h.comp_clm ((σ₀ (1 : A)).range.subtypeL)).clm_comp
    ((σ₁ (1 : A)).rangeRestrict)

end NonUnitalStarAlgHom

Author: @toskua

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Star.StarAlgHom
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Star.StarProjection
public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Adjoint
public import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Module.ContinuousLinearMap.Idempotent
public import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Module.ContinuousLinearMap.Restrict

/-!
# A unital representation on the actual range of the represented unit

A possibly nonunital complex star representation of a unital source algebra
restricts to a genuinely unital representation on the range of its unit image.
The support has the inherited Hilbert structure and completeness from the
closed range of the actual idempotent; no projector or new norm is constructed.
The source algebra need not be normed or complete. Zero support is permitted.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace NonUnitalStarAlgHom

universe uA uH

variable {A : Type uA} [Semiring A] [Algebra ℂ A] [StarRing A]
variable {H : Type uH} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]

/-- Restrict a possibly nonunital complex star representation to the actual
range of its represented unit. The resulting representation is unital there. -/
noncomputable def unitRangeStarAlgHom (σ : A →⋆ₙₐ[ℂ] (H →L[ℂ] H)) :
    letI : CompleteSpace (σ (1 : A)).range :=
      (ContinuousLinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.isClosed_range
        ((IsStarProjection.one A).map σ).isIdempotentElem).completeSpace_coe;
    A →⋆ₐ[ℂ] ((σ (1 : A)).range →L[ℂ] (σ (1 : A)).range) := by
  let : CompleteSpace (σ (1 : A)).range :=
    (ContinuousLinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.isClosed_range
        ((IsStarProjection.one A).map σ).isIdempotentElem).completeSpace_coe
  let p : H →L[ℂ] H := σ (1 : A)
  let E : Submodule ℂ H := p.range
  have hp : IsStarProjection p := (IsStarProjection.one A).map σ
  have hMem (a : A) (x : H) : σ a x ∈ E := by
    refine ⟨σ a x, ?_⟩
    have hpa : p * σ a = σ a := by
      change σ (1 : A) * σ a = σ a
      rw [← map_mul σ (1 : A) a, one_mul]
    exact congrArg (fun T : H →L[ℂ] H => T x) hpa
  have hFix (x : E) : p (x : H) = (x : H) :=
    (LinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.isProj_range p.toLinearMap
      (ContinuousLinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.toLinearMap hp.isIdempotentElem)).map_id
      (x : H) x.property
  let r (a : A) : E →L[ℂ] E :=
    (σ a).restrict (fun x _ => hMem a x)
  exact
    { toFun a := (σ a).restrict (fun x _ => hMem a x)
      map_zero' := by
        apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
        intro x
        apply Subtype.ext
        change σ (0 : A) (x : H) = 0
        exact congrArg (fun T : H →L[ℂ] H => T (x : H)) (map_zero σ)
      map_add' a b := by
        apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
        intro x
        apply Subtype.ext
        change σ (a + b) (x : H) = σ a (x : H) + σ b (x : H)
        exact congrArg (fun T : H →L[ℂ] H => T (x : H)) (map_add σ a b)
      map_one' := by
        apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
        intro x
        apply Subtype.ext
        change p (x : H) = (x : H)
        exact hFix x
      map_mul' a b := by
        apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
        intro x
        apply Subtype.ext
        change σ (a * b) (x : H) = σ a (σ b (x : H))
        exact congrArg (fun T : H →L[ℂ] H => T (x : H)) (map_mul σ a b)
      commutes' z := by
        apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
        intro x
        apply Subtype.ext
        change σ (algebraMap ℂ A z) (x : H) = z • (x : H)
        rw [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one, map_smul]
        change z • p (x : H) = z • (x : H)
        exact congrArg (fun y : H => z • y) (hFix x)
      map_star' a := by
        change r (star a) = star (r a)
        rw [ContinuousLinearMap.star_eq_adjoint]
        apply (ContinuousLinearMap.eq_adjoint_iff _ _).2
        intro x y
        change inner ℂ (σ (star a) (x : H)) (y : H) =
          inner ℂ (x : H) (σ a (y : H))
        rw [map_star σ a, ContinuousLinearMap.star_eq_adjoint]
        exact ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left (σ a) (y : H) (x : H) }

/-- The included-vector action of the support representation is exactly
the original represented operator, not a newly chosen compression value. -/
@[simp]
theorem unitRangeStarAlgHom_apply (σ : A →⋆ₙₐ[ℂ] (H →L[ℂ] H))
    (a : A) (x : (σ (1 : A)).range) :
    letI : CompleteSpace (σ (1 : A)).range :=
      (ContinuousLinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.isClosed_range
        ((IsStarProjection.one A).map σ).isIdempotentElem).completeSpace_coe;
    (unitRangeStarAlgHom σ a x : H) = σ a (x : H) := by
  let : CompleteSpace (σ (1 : A)).range :=
    (ContinuousLinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.isClosed_range
        ((IsStarProjection.one A).map σ).isIdempotentElem).completeSpace_coe
  rfl

end NonUnitalStarAlgHom

Author: @toskua

module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct.CompletionMap

/-!
# Adjoints of maps on completed Hilbert tensors

The adjoint identity is proved using the original algebraic tensor inner
product and its dense image in the stock completion. Factor Hilbert spaces
are complete; the algebraic tensor has no completeness hypothesis.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open UniformSpace
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe u𝕜 uE₁ uE₂ uF₁ uF₂

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {E₁ : Type uE₁} [NormedAddCommGroup E₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₁]
variable {E₂ : Type uE₂} [NormedAddCommGroup E₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₂]
variable {F₁ : Type uF₁} [NormedAddCommGroup F₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₁]
variable {F₂ : Type uF₂} [NormedAddCommGroup F₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₂]
variable [CompleteSpace E₁] [CompleteSpace E₂]
variable [CompleteSpace F₁] [CompleteSpace F₂]

/-- The actual Hilbert-space adjoint on the completed tensor is the tensor
map of the factor adjoints. -/
@[simp]
theorem adjoint_mapLCompletion (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    (mapLCompletion f g).adjoint = mapLCompletion f.adjoint g.adjoint := by
  have hAlg (v : E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂) (u : E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) :
      inner 𝕜 (mapL f.adjoint g.adjoint v) u = inner 𝕜 v (mapL f g u) := by
    refine v.inductionOn ?_ ?_
    · intro vE vF
      refine u.inductionOn ?_ ?_
      · intro uE uF
        simp only [mapL_tmul, inner_tmul, ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left]
      · intro u₁ u₂ h₁ h₂
        simp only [map_add, inner_add_right, h₁, h₂]
    · intro v₁ v₂ h₁ h₂
      simp only [map_add, inner_add_left, h₁, h₂]
  apply Eq.symm
  refine (ContinuousLinearMap.eq_adjoint_iff
    (mapLCompletion f.adjoint g.adjoint) (mapLCompletion f g)).2 ?_
  intro v u
  refine Completion.induction_on₂ v u (isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro v₀ u₀
  simpa only [mapLCompletion_coe, Completion.inner_coe] using hAlg v₀ u₀

/-- For factor endomorphisms, the completed map preserves the operator star. -/
@[simp]
theorem star_mapLCompletion (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₁) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₁) :
    star (mapLCompletion f g) = mapLCompletion (star f) (star g) := by
  simpa only [ContinuousLinearMap.star_eq_adjoint] using adjoint_mapLCompletion f g

end TensorProduct

Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Completion
public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct

/-!
# Bounded maps on completed Hilbert tensors

The carrier is the stock uniform completion of the algebraic tensor equipped
with its stock inner-product norm. Bounded maps on the factors act on this
completion through `ContinuousLinearMap.completion`.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open UniformSpace
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe u𝕜 uE₁ uE₂ uE₃ uF₁ uF₂ uF₃

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {E₁ : Type uE₁} [NormedAddCommGroup E₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₁]
variable {E₂ : Type uE₂} [NormedAddCommGroup E₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₂]
variable {F₁ : Type uF₁} [NormedAddCommGroup F₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₁]
variable {F₂ : Type uF₂} [NormedAddCommGroup F₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₂]

/-- The bounded tensor map between the literal stock Hilbert completions. -/
def mapLCompletion (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) →L[𝕜] Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂) :=
  (mapL f g).completion

/-- The completed map extends the original bounded algebraic tensor map. -/
@[simp]
theorem mapLCompletion_coe (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂)
    (u : E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) :
    mapLCompletion f g (u : Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁)) =
      (mapL f g u : Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂)) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.completion_apply_coe (mapL f g) u

/-- On a pure tensor, the completed map applies the two factor maps. -/
theorem mapLCompletion_tmul (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂)
    (x : E₁) (y : F₁) :
    mapLCompletion f g (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁)) =
      (f x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] g y : Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂)) := by
  rw [mapLCompletion_coe, mapL_tmul]

/-- Completion retains the product upper bound for the operator norm. -/
theorem norm_mapLCompletion_le (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    ‖mapLCompletion f g‖ ≤ ‖f‖ * ‖g‖ := by
  refine (mapLCompletion f g).opNorm_le_bound
    (mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg f) (norm_nonneg g)) ?_
  intro z
  refine Completion.induction_on z (isClosed_le (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro u
  simpa only [mapLCompletion_coe, Completion.norm_coe] using
    (mapL f g).le_of_opNorm_le (norm_mapL_le f g) u

variable (𝕜 E₁ F₁) in
/-- Identity factor maps induce the identity on the completed tensor. -/
@[simp]
theorem mapLCompletion_id_id :
    mapLCompletion (ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 E₁) (ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 F₁) =
      ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 (Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁)) := by
  ext z
  refine Completion.induction_on z (isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro u
  simp only [mapLCompletion_coe, mapL_id_id, ContinuousLinearMap.id_apply]

/-- A zero first factor induces the zero completed tensor map. -/
@[simp]
theorem mapLCompletion_zero_left (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    mapLCompletion (0 : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) g = 0 := by
  ext z
  refine Completion.induction_on z (isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro u
  simp only [mapLCompletion_coe, mapL_zero_left, zero_apply,
    Completion.coe_zero]

/-- A zero second factor induces the zero completed tensor map. -/
@[simp]
theorem mapLCompletion_zero_right (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) :
    mapLCompletion f (0 : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) = 0 := by
  ext z
  refine Completion.induction_on z (isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro u
  simp only [mapLCompletion_coe, mapL_zero_right, zero_apply,
    Completion.coe_zero]

/-- The completed tensor map is additive in its first operator. -/
theorem mapLCompletion_add_left (f₁ f₂ : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    mapLCompletion (f₁ + f₂) g = mapLCompletion f₁ g + mapLCompletion f₂ g := by
  ext z
  refine Completion.induction_on z (isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro u
  simp only [mapLCompletion_coe, mapL_add_left, add_apply,
    Completion.coe_add]

/-- The completed tensor map is additive in its second operator. -/
theorem mapLCompletion_add_right (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g₁ g₂ : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    mapLCompletion f (g₁ + g₂) = mapLCompletion f g₁ + mapLCompletion f g₂ := by
  ext z
  refine Completion.induction_on z (isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro u
  simp only [mapLCompletion_coe, mapL_add_right, add_apply,
    Completion.coe_add]

/-- The completed tensor map is scalar linear in its first operator. -/
theorem mapLCompletion_smul_left (c : 𝕜) (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    mapLCompletion (c • f) g = c • mapLCompletion f g := by
  change (mapL (c • f) g).completion = c • (mapL f g).completion
  rw [mapL_smul_left]
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.coeFn_injective
  funext z
  change Completion.map (fun u : E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁ => c • mapL f g u) z =
    c • Completion.map (mapL f g) z
  rw [Completion.smul_def]
  exact (congr_fun (Completion.map_comp
    (uniformContinuous_const_smul c) (mapL f g).uniformContinuous) z).symm

/-- The completed tensor map is scalar linear in its second operator. -/
theorem mapLCompletion_smul_right (c : 𝕜) (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    mapLCompletion f (c • g) = c • mapLCompletion f g := by
  change (mapL f (c • g)).completion = c • (mapL f g).completion
  rw [mapL_smul_right]
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.coeFn_injective
  funext z
  change Completion.map (fun u : E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁ => c • mapL f g u) z =
    c • Completion.map (mapL f g) z
  rw [Completion.smul_def]
  exact (congr_fun (Completion.map_comp
    (uniformContinuous_const_smul c) (mapL f g).uniformContinuous) z).symm

section Composition

variable {E₃ : Type uE₃} [NormedAddCommGroup E₃] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₃]
variable {F₃ : Type uF₃} [NormedAddCommGroup F₃] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₃]

/-- Composition is performed separately in the two factors. -/
theorem mapLCompletion_comp (f₂ : E₂ →L[𝕜] E₃) (f₁ : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂)
    (g₂ : F₂ →L[𝕜] F₃) (g₁ : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    mapLCompletion (f₂.comp f₁) (g₂.comp g₁) =
      (mapLCompletion f₂ g₂).comp (mapLCompletion f₁ g₁) := by
  ext z
  refine Completion.induction_on z (isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)) ?_
  intro u
  simp only [mapLCompletion_coe, mapL_comp, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply]

end Composition

/-- Multiplication of factor endomorphisms becomes composition of completed maps. -/
theorem mapLCompletion_mul (f₁ f₂ : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₁) (g₁ g₂ : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₁) :
    mapLCompletion (f₁ * f₂) (g₁ * g₂) =
      mapLCompletion f₁ g₁ * mapLCompletion f₂ g₂ :=
  mapLCompletion_comp f₁ f₂ g₁ g₂

end TensorProduct

/-
Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Completion
public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct
public import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Module.Basic

/-!
# Dense coefficient tensor spans in the stock Hilbert completion

Two subsets with dense linear spans give a dense linear span of their
actual pure tensors. No completeness of the algebraic tensor is assumed.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open UniformSpace Set
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe u𝕜 uH uK

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {H : Type uH} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 H]
variable {K : Type uK} [NormedAddCommGroup K] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 K]

/-- Dense factor spans generate a dense span of their literal completed Hilbert tensors. -/
theorem dense_span_completed_tmul (s : Set H) (t : Set K)
    (hs : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 s : Set H))
    (ht : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 t : Set K)) :
    Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜
      {z : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K) | ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ t,
        z = (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K))} : Set (Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K))) := by
  let S : Submodule 𝕜 (Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)) := Submodule.span 𝕜
    {z : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K) | ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ t,
      z = (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K))}
  have hSpan {x : H} {y : K} (hx : x ∈ Submodule.span 𝕜 s)
      (hy : y ∈ Submodule.span 𝕜 t) :
      (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)) ∈ S.topologicalClosure := by
    refine Submodule.span_induction₂
      (p := fun x y _ _ =>
        (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)) ∈ S.topologicalClosure)
      ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ hx hy
    · intro x y hx hy
      exact S.le_topologicalClosure (Submodule.subset_span ⟨x, hx, y, hy, rfl⟩)
    · intro y _hy
      simpa only [zero_tmul, Completion.coe_zero] using S.topologicalClosure.zero_mem
    · intro x _hx
      simpa only [tmul_zero, Completion.coe_zero] using S.topologicalClosure.zero_mem
    · intro x y z _hx _hy _hz hx hy
      simpa only [add_tmul, Completion.coe_add] using S.topologicalClosure.add_mem hx hy
    · intro x y z _hx _hy _hz hy hz
      simpa only [tmul_add, Completion.coe_add] using S.topologicalClosure.add_mem hy hz
    · intro c x y _hx _hy hxy
      simpa only [← smul_tmul', Completion.coe_smul] using
        S.topologicalClosure.smul_mem c hxy
    · intro c x y _hx _hy hxy
      simpa only [tmul_smul, Completion.coe_smul] using
        S.topologicalClosure.smul_mem c hxy
  have hLeft (y : K) (hy : y ∈ Submodule.span 𝕜 t) (x : H) :
      (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)) ∈ S.topologicalClosure := by
    have hc : Continuous fun x : H => (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)) :=
      (Completion.continuous_coe (H ⊗[𝕜] K)).comp
        ((continuous_tmul (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := H) (F := K)).comp
          (continuous_id.prodMk continuous_const))
    exact hs.induction (fun x hx => hSpan hx hy)
      (S.isClosed_topologicalClosure.preimage hc) x
  have hPure (x : H) (y : K) :
      (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)) ∈ S.topologicalClosure := by
    have hc : Continuous fun y : K => (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (H ⊗[𝕜] K)) :=
      (Completion.continuous_coe (H ⊗[𝕜] K)).comp
        ((continuous_tmul (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := H) (F := K)).comp
          (continuous_const.prodMk continuous_id))
    exact ht.induction (fun y hy => hLeft y hy x)
      (S.isClosed_topologicalClosure.preimage hc) y
  apply Submodule.dense_iff_topologicalClosure_eq_top.mpr
  apply Submodule.eq_top_iff'.mpr
  intro z
  refine Completion.induction_on z S.isClosed_topologicalClosure ?_
  intro w
  induction w using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | tmul x y => exact hPure x y
  | add w v hw hv =>
    simpa only [Completion.coe_add] using S.topologicalClosure.add_mem hw hv

end TensorProduct

module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct.CyclicCompletion
public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Completion
public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Extend

/-!
# Moving an actual completion inside the original Hilbert tensor

The original completion inclusion tensors with identity. Its completed stock
isometry has dense range by actual dense coefficient spans, hence is onto.
These are the inside-completion constructor fields needed for the original
mixed-factor Radon L2 carrier. Zero factors and independent universes remain.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open Filter Set UniformSpace
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

noncomputable section

universe u𝕜 uE uF

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {E : Type uE} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E]
variable {F : Type uF} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F]

/-- The actual stock inclusion of a factor into its original uniform completion. -/
def factorCompletionInclusion : E →ₗᵢ[𝕜] Completion E := by
  let _ : UniformContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 E :=
    uniformContinuousConstSMul_of_continuousConstSMul 𝕜 E
  exact Completion.toComplₗᵢ

/-- Tensor the original left completion inclusion with identity, then complete that actual map. -/
def completionLeftTensorEmbedding :
    Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F) →ₗᵢ[𝕜] Completion ((Completion E) ⊗[𝕜] F) :=
  (mapIsometry (factorCompletionInclusion (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E)) (LinearIsometry.id : F →ₗᵢ[𝕜] F)).completion

/-- The actual left inside-completion map retains the literal original completed pure tensor. -/
theorem completionLeftTensorEmbedding_tmul (x : E) (y : F) :
    completionLeftTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜)
        ((x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : E ⊗[𝕜] F) : Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F)) =
      (((x : Completion E) ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : (Completion E) ⊗[𝕜] F) :
        Completion ((Completion E) ⊗[𝕜] F)) := by
  rw [completionLeftTensorEmbedding, LinearIsometry.completion_apply_coe]
  simp only [mapIsometry_apply, TensorProduct.map_tmul, LinearIsometry.id_apply]
  rfl

/-- The actual completed left inclusion has dense range in the original target completion. -/
theorem denseRange_completionLeftTensorEmbedding :
    DenseRange (completionLeftTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)) := by
  let s : Set (Completion E) := range ((↑) : E → Completion E)
  let t : Set F := univ
  have hs : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 s : Set (Completion E)) := by
    intro x
    exact (closure_mono Submodule.subset_span) (Completion.denseRange_coe x)
  have ht : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 t : Set F) := by
    simpa only [t, Submodule.span_univ, Submodule.top_coe] using (dense_univ : Dense (univ : Set F))
  let P : Set (Completion ((Completion E) ⊗[𝕜] F)) :=
    {z | ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ t,
      z = (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion ((Completion E) ⊗[𝕜] F))}
  have hP : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 P : Set (Completion ((Completion E) ⊗[𝕜] F))) :=
    dense_span_completed_tmul s t hs ht
  have hSpan : Submodule.span 𝕜 P ≤
      (completionLeftTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)).toLinearMap.range := by
    apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
    rintro z ⟨x, ⟨a, rfl⟩, y, _hy, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨((a ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : E ⊗[𝕜] F) : Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F)),
      completionLeftTensorEmbedding_tmul a y⟩
  intro z
  exact (closure_mono hSpan) (hP z)

/-- Actual density and complete-source isometry prove the left inside-completion map is onto. -/
theorem surjective_completionLeftTensorEmbedding :
    Function.Surjective (completionLeftTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)) := by
  let I := completionLeftTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)
  have hclosed : IsClosed (range I) := I.isometry.isClosedEmbedding.isClosed_range
  intro z
  have hz : z ∈ closure (range I) := denseRange_completionLeftTensorEmbedding z
  rw [hclosed.closure_eq] at hz
  exact hz

/-- The original stock tensor completion equals the tensor with its left factor completed inside. -/
def completionLeftTensorUnitary :
    Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F) ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] Completion ((Completion E) ⊗[𝕜] F) :=
  LinearIsometryEquiv.ofSurjective (completionLeftTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜))
    (surjective_completionLeftTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜))

/-- Tensor identity with the original right completion inclusion, then complete the actual map. -/
def completionRightTensorEmbedding :
    Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F) →ₗᵢ[𝕜] Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] (Completion F)) :=
  (mapIsometry (LinearIsometry.id : E →ₗᵢ[𝕜] E) (factorCompletionInclusion (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := F))).completion

/-- The actual right inside-completion map retains the literal original completed pure tensor. -/
theorem completionRightTensorEmbedding_tmul (x : E) (y : F) :
    completionRightTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜)
        ((x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : E ⊗[𝕜] F) : Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F)) =
      ((x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] (y : Completion F) : E ⊗[𝕜] (Completion F)) :
        Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] (Completion F))) := by
  rw [completionRightTensorEmbedding, LinearIsometry.completion_apply_coe]
  simp only [mapIsometry_apply, TensorProduct.map_tmul, LinearIsometry.id_apply]
  rfl

/-- Actual dense right coefficient spans give dense range of the original completed right map. -/
theorem denseRange_completionRightTensorEmbedding :
    DenseRange (completionRightTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)) := by
  let s : Set E := univ
  let t : Set (Completion F) := range ((↑) : F → Completion F)
  have hs : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 s : Set E) := by
    simpa only [s, Submodule.span_univ, Submodule.top_coe] using (dense_univ : Dense (univ : Set E))
  have ht : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 t : Set (Completion F)) := by
    intro y
    exact (closure_mono Submodule.subset_span) (Completion.denseRange_coe y)
  let P : Set (Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] (Completion F))) :=
    {z | ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ t,
      z = (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y : Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] (Completion F)))}
  have hP : Dense (Submodule.span 𝕜 P : Set (Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] (Completion F)))) :=
    dense_span_completed_tmul s t hs ht
  have hSpan : Submodule.span 𝕜 P ≤
      (completionRightTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)).toLinearMap.range := by
    apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
    rintro z ⟨x, _hx, y, ⟨b, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨((x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] b : E ⊗[𝕜] F) : Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F)),
      completionRightTensorEmbedding_tmul x b⟩
  intro z
  exact (closure_mono hSpan) (hP z)

/-- The actual completed right inclusion is onto by complete-source isometry and proved density. -/
theorem surjective_completionRightTensorEmbedding :
    Function.Surjective (completionRightTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)) := by
  let I := completionRightTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F)
  have hclosed : IsClosed (range I) := I.isometry.isClosedEmbedding.isClosed_range
  intro z
  have hz : z ∈ closure (range I) := denseRange_completionRightTensorEmbedding z
  rw [hclosed.closure_eq] at hz
  exact hz

/-- The original stock tensor completion equals the tensor with its right factor completed inside. -/
def completionRightTensorUnitary :
    Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F) ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] (Completion F)) :=
  LinearIsometryEquiv.ofSurjective (completionRightTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜))
    (surjective_completionRightTensorEmbedding (𝕜 := 𝕜))

end

end TensorProduct

Author: @toskua

module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct.CompletionMap
public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.HomInjective
public import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Module.ContinuousLinearMap.Basic

/-!
# Faithfulness of the actual completed tensor operator action

The tensor lift of the bounded factor maps acts on the stock Hilbert tensor
completion. Its values on the actual raw core agree with the canonical
algebraic tensor action of the underlying linear maps. Raw faithfulness and
the genuine completion inclusion then prove injectivity, including zero
factor spaces. No norm comparison or completed-model certificate is supplied.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open UniformSpace
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace TensorProduct

universe u𝕜 uE₁ uE₂ uF₁ uF₂

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {E₁ : Type uE₁} [NormedAddCommGroup E₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₁]
variable {E₂ : Type uE₂} [NormedAddCommGroup E₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E₂]
variable {F₁ : Type uF₁} [NormedAddCommGroup F₁] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₁]
variable {F₂ : Type uF₂} [NormedAddCommGroup F₂] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F₂]

/-- The actual linear tensor lift of the bounded completed factor-map action. -/
noncomputable def mapLCompletionLinear :
    (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) ⊗[𝕜] (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) →ₗ[𝕜]
      Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) →L[𝕜] Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂) :=
  TensorProduct.lift
    { toFun := fun f =>
        { toFun := fun g => mapLCompletion f g
          map_add' g h := mapLCompletion_add_right f g h
          map_smul' c g := mapLCompletion_smul_right c f g }
      map_add' f h := by
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro g
        exact mapLCompletion_add_left f h g
      map_smul' c f := by
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro g
        exact mapLCompletion_smul_left c f g }

/-- A pure tensor of bounded operators has the original completed tensor action. -/
theorem mapLCompletionLinear_tmul (f : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) (g : F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) :
    mapLCompletionLinear (f ⊗ₜ[𝕜] g) = mapLCompletion f g := rfl

/-- The actual completed action retains the canonical raw algebraic operator value. -/
theorem mapLCompletionLinear_coe
    (z : (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) ⊗[𝕜] (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂)) (u : E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) :
    mapLCompletionLinear z (u : Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁)) =
      (homTensorHomMap (RingHom.id 𝕜) E₁ F₁ E₂ F₂
        (TensorProduct.map (ContinuousLinearMap.coeLM 𝕜) (ContinuousLinearMap.coeLM 𝕜) z) u :
          Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂)) := by
  induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
  | tmul f g =>
    simp only [mapLCompletionLinear_tmul, mapLCompletion_coe, map_tmul,
      homTensorHomMap_apply, mapL_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.coeLM_apply]
  | add z w hz hw =>
    simp only [map_add, _root_.add_apply, LinearMap.add_apply,
      Completion.coe_add, hz, hw]

/-- Finite tensors of bounded maps act faithfully on the original completed Hilbert tensor. -/
theorem mapLCompletionLinear_injective :
    Function.Injective
      (mapLCompletionLinear : (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) ⊗[𝕜] (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) →ₗ[𝕜]
        Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁) →L[𝕜] Completion (E₂ ⊗[𝕜] F₂)) := by
  classical
  let f : (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) →ₗ[𝕜] E₁ →ₗ[𝕜] E₂ := ContinuousLinearMap.coeLM 𝕜
  let g : (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂) →ₗ[𝕜] F₁ →ₗ[𝕜] F₂ := ContinuousLinearMap.coeLM 𝕜
  have hf : LinearMap.ker f = ⊥ := LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mpr ContinuousLinearMap.coe_injective
  have hg : LinearMap.ker g = ⊥ := LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mpr ContinuousLinearMap.coe_injective
  have hleft (z : (E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂) ⊗[𝕜] (F₁ →L[𝕜] F₂)) :
      TensorProduct.map f.leftInverse g.leftInverse (TensorProduct.map f g z) = z := by
    induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
    | tmul u v =>
      rw [map_tmul, map_tmul, LinearMap.leftInverse_apply_of_inj hf,
        LinearMap.leftInverse_apply_of_inj hg]
    | add z w hz hw =>
      rw [map_add, map_add, hz, hw]
  have hmap : Function.Injective (TensorProduct.map f g) := by
    intro z w h
    have h' := congrArg (TensorProduct.map f.leftInverse g.leftInverse) h
    simpa only [hleft] using h'
  intro z w h
  apply hmap
  apply homTensorHomMap_injective
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro u
  apply Completion.coe_injective
  have hcore := DFunLike.congr_fun h (u : Completion (E₁ ⊗[𝕜] F₁))
  simpa only [mapLCompletionLinear_coe] using hcore

end TensorProduct

Author: @toskua

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.l2Space
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Submodule.Map
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.LinearPMap
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Pi

/-!
# Unbounded diagonal operators for a supplied Hilbert basis

Arbitrary scalar weights define a partial linear operator on precisely those
vectors whose weighted basis coefficients belong to `ℓ²`. Its value is the
inverse basis representation of that actual `ℓ²` vector. No bound on the
weights or nonempty-index hypothesis is imposed.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open scoped ENNReal InnerProductSpace

namespace HilbertBasis

universe uI uK uH

variable {ι : Type uI} {𝕜 : Type uK} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {H : Type uH} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 H]
variable (e : HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 H) (α : ι → 𝕜)

/-- The unrestricted weighted basis coordinates as a linear map into all scalar families. -/
def diagonalCoordinateLinearMap : H →ₗ[𝕜] (ι → 𝕜) :=
  LinearMap.pi fun i =>
    α i • ((lp.evalₗ (𝕜 := 𝕜) (fun _ : ι => 𝕜) 2 i).comp e.repr.toLinearMap)

/-- Every raw coordinate is the original scalar weight times the supplied basis coefficient. -/
@[simp]
theorem diagonalCoordinateLinearMap_apply (h : H) (i : ι) :
    diagonalCoordinateLinearMap e α h i = α i * e.repr h i := rfl

/-- The maximal domain on which the weighted basis coefficients are square summable. -/
def unboundedDiagonalDomain : Submodule 𝕜 H :=
  (lpSubmodule 𝕜 (fun _ : ι => 𝕜) 2).comap (diagonalCoordinateLinearMap e α)

/-- Membership in the domain is exactly square summability of the weighted coordinates. -/
theorem mem_unboundedDiagonalDomain_iff (h : H) :
    h ∈ unboundedDiagonalDomain e α ↔
      Summable fun i => ‖α i * ⟪e i, h⟫_𝕜‖ ^ 2 := by
  change Memℓp (fun i => α i * e.repr h i) (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ↔ _
  have htwo : 0 < (2 : ℝ≥0∞).toReal := by simp
  simpa only [ENNReal.toReal_ofNat, Real.rpow_two, HilbertBasis.repr_apply_apply] using
    (memℓp_gen_iff (p := (2 : ℝ≥0∞)) (f := fun i => α i * e.repr h i) htwo)

/-- The actual square-summable weighted coordinate vector, as a linear map on the domain. -/
def unboundedDiagonalLp : unboundedDiagonalDomain e α →ₗ[𝕜] lp (fun _ : ι => 𝕜) 2 :=
  (diagonalCoordinateLinearMap e α).submoduleComap (lpSubmodule 𝕜 (fun _ : ι => 𝕜) 2)

/-- The coordinate vector retains the original weight and supplied basis coefficient. -/
@[simp]
theorem unboundedDiagonalLp_apply (x : unboundedDiagonalDomain e α) (i : ι) :
    unboundedDiagonalLp e α x i = α i * e.repr (x : H) i := rfl

/-- The diagonal partial linear map on its full square-summability domain. -/
def unboundedDiagonal : H →ₗ.[𝕜] H :=
  LinearPMap.mk (unboundedDiagonalDomain e α)
    (e.repr.symm.toLinearMap.comp (unboundedDiagonalLp e α))

/-- The partial map has precisely the maximal weighted-coordinate domain. -/
@[simp]
theorem unboundedDiagonal_domain :
    (unboundedDiagonal e α).domain = unboundedDiagonalDomain e α := rfl

/-- The value is the supplied basis reconstruction of the actual weighted coordinate vector. -/
@[simp]
theorem unboundedDiagonal_apply (x : unboundedDiagonalDomain e α) :
    unboundedDiagonal e α x = e.repr.symm (unboundedDiagonalLp e α x) := rfl

/-- Every basis coordinate is multiplied by its original scalar weight. -/
theorem unboundedDiagonal_repr_apply (x : unboundedDiagonalDomain e α) (i : ι) :
    e.repr (unboundedDiagonal e α x) i = α i * e.repr (x : H) i := by
  rw [unboundedDiagonal_apply, e.repr.apply_symm_apply]
  exact unboundedDiagonalLp_apply e α x i

/-- The defining Hilbert series converges to the actual partial-map value. -/
theorem unboundedDiagonal_hasSum (x : unboundedDiagonalDomain e α) :
    HasSum (fun i => (α i * ⟪e i, (x : H)⟫_𝕜) • e i) (unboundedDiagonal e α x) := by
  simpa only [unboundedDiagonal_apply, unboundedDiagonalLp_apply,
    HilbertBasis.repr_apply_apply] using e.hasSum_repr_symm (unboundedDiagonalLp e α x)

/-- The convergent defining series evaluates to the diagonal operator. -/
theorem unboundedDiagonal_eq_tsum (x : unboundedDiagonalDomain e α) :
    unboundedDiagonal e α x = ∑' i, (α i * ⟪e i, (x : H)⟫_𝕜) • e i :=
  (unboundedDiagonal_hasSum e α x).tsum_eq.symm

/-- Zero weights give the entire original space as the domain. -/
@[simp]
theorem unboundedDiagonalDomain_zero : unboundedDiagonalDomain e (0 : ι → 𝕜) = ⊤ := by
  ext h
  simp [mem_unboundedDiagonalDomain_iff]

/-- Zero weights give the zero vector at every point of the actual domain. -/
theorem unboundedDiagonal_zero_apply (x : unboundedDiagonalDomain e (0 : ι → 𝕜)) :
    unboundedDiagonal e (0 : ι → 𝕜) x = 0 := by
  apply e.repr.injective
  apply lp.ext
  funext i
  simp

end HilbertBasis

end

/-
Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.l2Space
public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Adjoint
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Compact.Basic
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Fredholm.Basic

import Mathlib.Analysis.RCLike.Lemmas
import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum

/-!
# The unilateral shift on `ℓ²`

This file defines the forward unilateral shift on the canonical Mathlib carrier
`lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2`. It inserts zero in the zeroth coordinate and moves
each existing coordinate one place to the right.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

namespace lp

universe u v

variable {𝕜 : Type u} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable {G : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup G] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 G]
  [hG : CompleteSpace G]

/-- The coordinate function underlying the forward unilateral shift. -/
def unilateralShiftSeq (x : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2) : ℕ → G
  | 0 => 0
  | n + 1 => x n

omit hG in
@[simp]
theorem unilateralShiftSeq_zero (x : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2) :
    unilateralShiftSeq x 0 = 0 :=
  rfl

omit hG in
@[simp]
theorem unilateralShiftSeq_succ (x : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2) (n : ℕ) :
    unilateralShiftSeq x (n + 1) = x n :=
  rfl

omit hG in
theorem unilateralShiftSeq_mem (x : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2) :
    Memℓp (unilateralShiftSeq x) 2 := by
  have hp : 0 < (2 : ENNReal).toReal := by norm_num
  have hx : Summable (fun n => ‖x n‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal) :=
    (memℓp_gen_iff hp).mp (lp.memℓp x)
  have hshift :
      (fun n => ‖unilateralShiftSeq x (n + 1)‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal) =
        fun n => ‖x n‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal := by
    funext n
    rfl
  have htail :
      Summable (fun n => ‖unilateralShiftSeq x (n + 1)‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal) := by
    rw [hshift]
    exact hx
  exact memℓp_gen ((summable_nat_add_iff 1).mp htail)

omit hG in
private theorem unilateralShiftSeq_norm (x : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2) :
    ‖(⟨unilateralShiftSeq x, unilateralShiftSeq_mem x⟩ :
        lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2)‖ = ‖x‖ := by
  have hp : 0 < (2 : ENNReal).toReal := by norm_num
  have hx : Summable (fun n => ‖x n‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal) :=
    (memℓp_gen_iff hp).mp (lp.memℓp x)
  have hshift :
      (fun n => ‖unilateralShiftSeq x (n + 1)‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal) =
        fun n => ‖x n‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal := by
    funext n
    rfl
  have htail :
      Summable (fun n => ‖unilateralShiftSeq x (n + 1)‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal) := by
    rw [hshift]
    exact hx
  have hsum : Summable (fun n => ‖unilateralShiftSeq x n‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal) :=
    (summable_nat_add_iff 1).mp htail
  have hzero : ‖unilateralShiftSeq x 0‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal = 0 := by
    calc
      ‖unilateralShiftSeq x 0‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal =
          ‖(0 : G)‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal := by rw [unilateralShiftSeq_zero]
      _ = (0 : ℝ) ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal := by
        have hnorm : ‖(0 : G)‖ = 0 := _root_.norm_zero
        rw [hnorm]
      _ = 0 := Real.zero_rpow (ne_of_gt hp)
  have hrange :
      ∑ n ∈ Finset.range 1,
          ‖unilateralShiftSeq x n‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal = 0 := by
    rw [Finset.sum_range_one]
    exact hzero
  have hadd := Summable.sum_add_tsum_nat_add 1 hsum
  rw [hrange, zero_add] at hadd
  have htailSum :
      (∑' n, ‖unilateralShiftSeq x (n + 1)‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal) =
        ∑' n, ‖x n‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal := by
    rw [hshift]
  have hsumEq :
      (∑' n, ‖unilateralShiftSeq x n‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal) =
        ∑' n, ‖x n‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal := by
    rw [← hadd, htailSum]
  have hnormShift :
      ‖(⟨unilateralShiftSeq x, unilateralShiftSeq_mem x⟩ :
          lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2)‖ =
        ((∑' n, ‖unilateralShiftSeq x n‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal) ^
          ((1 : ℝ) / (2 : ENNReal).toReal)) := by
    rw [lp.norm_eq_tsum_rpow hp]
  have hnormInput :
      ‖x‖ = ((∑' n, ‖x n‖ ^ (2 : ENNReal).toReal) ^
        ((1 : ℝ) / (2 : ENNReal).toReal)) := by
    rw [lp.norm_eq_tsum_rpow hp]
  rw [hnormShift, hnormInput, hsumEq]

/-- The linear map underlying the unilateral shift. -/
def unilateralShiftLinear :
    lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 →ₗ[𝕜] lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 where
  toFun x := ⟨unilateralShiftSeq x, unilateralShiftSeq_mem x⟩
  map_add' x y := by
    apply lp.ext
    funext n
    cases n with
    | zero =>
      simp only [unilateralShiftSeq_zero, lp.coeFn_add, Pi.add_apply, add_zero]
    | succ n =>
      simp only [unilateralShiftSeq_succ, lp.coeFn_add, Pi.add_apply]
  map_smul' c x := by
    apply lp.ext
    funext n
    cases n with
    | zero =>
      simp only [unilateralShiftSeq_zero, lp.coeFn_smul, Pi.smul_apply, smul_zero]
    | succ n =>
      simp only [unilateralShiftSeq_succ, lp.coeFn_smul, Pi.smul_apply, RingHom.id_apply]

omit hG in
theorem unilateralShiftLinear_norm (x : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2) :
    ‖unilateralShiftLinear (𝕜 := 𝕜) x‖ = ‖x‖ := by
  have h : unilateralShiftLinear (𝕜 := 𝕜) x =
      (⟨unilateralShiftSeq x, unilateralShiftSeq_mem x⟩ :
        lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2) := rfl
  rw [h]
  exact unilateralShiftSeq_norm x

/-- The forward unilateral shift on `ℓ²(ℕ, G)`.

It sends `(x 0, x 1, ...)` to `(0, x 0, x 1, ...)`. -/
noncomputable def unilateralShift :
    lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 →L[𝕜] lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 :=
  unilateralShiftLinear.mkContinuous 1 fun x ↦ by
    rw [unilateralShiftLinear_norm, one_mul]

omit hG in
/-- The zeroth coordinate of the unilateral shift is zero. -/
@[simp]
theorem unilateralShift_apply_zero (x : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2) :
    unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) x 0 = 0 := by
  have h : unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) x =
      unilateralShiftLinear (𝕜 := 𝕜) x := rfl
  rw [h]
  exact unilateralShiftSeq_zero x

omit hG in
/-- The successor coordinates of the unilateral shift recover the input coordinates. -/
@[simp]
theorem unilateralShift_apply_succ (x : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2) (n : ℕ) :
    unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) x (n + 1) = x n := by
  have h : unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) x =
      unilateralShiftLinear (𝕜 := 𝕜) x := rfl
  rw [h]
  exact unilateralShiftSeq_succ x n

omit hG in
/-- The unilateral shift moves the `n`-th standard single to the `(n+1)`-st. -/
@[simp]
theorem unilateralShift_single (n : ℕ) (g : G) :
    unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (lp.single (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 n g) =
      lp.single (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 (n + 1) g := by
  apply lp.ext
  funext j
  cases j with
  | zero =>
    rw [unilateralShift_apply_zero]
    rw [lp.single_apply_ne (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 (n + 1) g
      (Nat.zero_ne_add_one n)]
  | succ j =>
    rw [unilateralShift_apply_succ]
    by_cases h : j = n
    · subst h
      rw [lp.single_apply_self, lp.single_apply_self]
    · have h' : j + 1 ≠ n + 1 := Nat.succ_ne_succ_iff.mpr h
      rw [lp.single_apply_ne (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 n g h]
      rw [lp.single_apply_ne (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 (n + 1) g h']

omit hG in
/-- The unilateral shift preserves the `ℓ²` norm. -/
theorem unilateralShift_norm (x : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2) :
    ‖unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) x‖ = ‖x‖ := by
  have h : unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) x =
      unilateralShiftLinear (𝕜 := 𝕜) x := rfl
  rw [h]
  exact unilateralShiftLinear_norm x

omit hG in
/-- The unilateral shift is an isometry. -/
theorem unilateralShift_isometry :
    Isometry (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)) :=
  (AddMonoidHomClass.isometry_iff_norm _).mpr unilateralShift_norm

omit hG in
/-- The unilateral shift is injective. -/
theorem unilateralShift_injective :
    Function.Injective (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)) :=
  (unilateralShift_isometry (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)).injective

/-- The range of the unilateral shift is closed. -/
theorem unilateralShift_isClosed_range :
    IsClosed (Set.range (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G))) :=
  (unilateralShift_isometry (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)).isClosedEmbedding.isClosed_range

omit hG in
/-- The unilateral shift is not surjective when its multiplicity space is nontrivial. -/
theorem unilateralShift_not_surjective [Nontrivial G] :
    ¬ Function.Surjective (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)) := by
  intro hsurj
  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := exists_ne (0 : G)
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ :=
    hsurj (lp.single (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 0 g)
  apply hg
  simpa using (congrArg (fun y => y 0) hx).symm

/-- The backward unilateral shift, defined as the Hilbert-space adjoint of the forward shift. -/
noncomputable abbrev backwardShift :
    lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 →L[𝕜] lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G))

/-- The backward shift removes the zeroth coordinate and moves every later coordinate left. -/
@[simp]
theorem backwardShift_apply (x : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2) (n : ℕ) :
    backwardShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) x n = x (n + 1) := by
  apply ext_inner_left 𝕜
  intro g
  calc
    inner 𝕜 g (backwardShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) x n) =
        inner 𝕜 (lp.single (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 n g)
          (backwardShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) x) :=
      (lp.inner_single_left (𝕜 := 𝕜) n g
        (backwardShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) x)).symm
    _ = inner 𝕜 (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜)
        (lp.single (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 n g)) x :=
      ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right _ _ _
    _ = inner 𝕜 (lp.single (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 (n + 1) g) x := by
      rw [unilateralShift_single]
    _ = inner 𝕜 g (x (n + 1)) :=
      lp.inner_single_left (𝕜 := 𝕜) (n + 1) g x

/-- The backward shift kills a standard single in the zeroth coordinate. -/
@[simp]
theorem backwardShift_single_zero (g : G) :
    backwardShift (𝕜 := 𝕜)
        (lp.single (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 0 g) = 0 := by
  apply lp.ext
  funext j
  rw [backwardShift_apply]
  rw [lp.single_apply_ne (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 0 g
    (Nat.succ_ne_zero j)]
  rfl

/-- The backward shift moves a successor standard single one coordinate left. -/
@[simp]
theorem backwardShift_single_succ (n : ℕ) (g : G) :
    backwardShift (𝕜 := 𝕜)
        (lp.single (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 (n + 1) g) =
      lp.single (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 n g := by
  apply lp.ext
  funext j
  rw [backwardShift_apply]
  by_cases h : j = n
  · subst h
    rw [lp.single_apply_self, lp.single_apply_self]
  · have h' : j + 1 ≠ n + 1 := Nat.succ_ne_succ_iff.mpr h
    rw [lp.single_apply_ne (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 (n + 1) g h']
    rw [lp.single_apply_ne (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 n g h]

/-- The backward shift is a left inverse of the forward unilateral shift. -/
@[simp]
theorem backwardShift_comp_unilateralShift :
    backwardShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) ∘L
      unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) = 1 :=
  (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)).norm_map_iff_adjoint_comp_self.mp
    unilateralShift_norm

/-- The backward unilateral shift is surjective. -/
theorem backwardShift_surjective :
    Function.Surjective (backwardShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)) := by
  intro x
  refine ⟨unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) x, ?_⟩
  have h := congrArg
    (fun T : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 →L[𝕜] lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 ↦ T x)
    (backwardShift_comp_unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G))
  change backwardShift (𝕜 := 𝕜)
      (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) x) = x at h
  exact h

/-- Projection onto the zeroth-coordinate defect of the unilateral shift. -/
noncomputable def unilateralShiftDefectProjection :
    lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 →L[𝕜] lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 :=
  1 - unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) ∘L
    backwardShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)

/-- The defect projection preserves the zeroth coordinate. -/
@[simp]
theorem unilateralShiftDefectProjection_apply_zero
    (x : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2) :
    unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) x 0 = x 0 := by
  simp [unilateralShiftDefectProjection, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply]

/-- Every successor coordinate of the defect projection vanishes. -/
@[simp]
theorem unilateralShiftDefectProjection_apply_succ
    (x : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2) (n : ℕ) :
    unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) x (n + 1) = 0 := by
  simp [unilateralShiftDefectProjection, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply]

/-- The forward shift followed by the backward shift is the complement of the defect. -/
@[simp]
theorem unilateralShift_comp_backwardShift :
    unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) ∘L
      backwardShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) =
        1 - unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) := by
  simp [unilateralShiftDefectProjection]

/-- A vector lies in the defect range exactly when all its successor coordinates vanish. -/
theorem mem_unilateralShiftDefectProjection_range_iff
    (x : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2) :
    x ∈ (unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)).range ↔
      ∀ n : ℕ, x (n + 1) = 0 := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨y, rfl⟩ n
    simp
  · intro hx
    refine ⟨x, ?_⟩
    apply lp.ext
    funext n
    cases n with
    | zero => simp
    | succ n => simpa using (hx n).symm

/-- The kernel of the defect projection is exactly the range of the unilateral shift. -/
theorem unilateralShiftDefectProjection_ker :
    (unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)).ker =
      (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)).range := by
  ext x
  constructor
  · intro hx
    change unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) x = 0 at hx
    refine ⟨backwardShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) x, ?_⟩
    have h := congrArg
      (fun T : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 →L[𝕜] lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 ↦ T x)
      (unilateralShift_comp_backwardShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G))
    change unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜)
        (backwardShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) x) =
      x - unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) x at h
    rw [hx, sub_zero] at h
    exact h
  · rintro ⟨y, rfl⟩
    change unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜)
      (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) y) = 0
    apply lp.ext
    funext n
    cases n <;> simp

/-- The zeroth-coordinate defect operator is a self-adjoint projection. -/
theorem unilateralShiftDefectProjection_isStarProjection :
    IsStarProjection
      (unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)) where
  isIdempotentElem := by
    change unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) *
        unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) =
      unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro x
    apply lp.ext
    funext n
    cases n <;> simp [mul_apply_eq_comp]
  isSelfAdjoint := by
    rw [isSelfAdjoint_iff]
    have hP : unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) =
        1 - unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) *
          star (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)) := by
      rw [unilateralShiftDefectProjection,
        ContinuousLinearMap.star_eq_adjoint, ContinuousLinearMap.mul_def]
    rw [hP]
    change ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint
        (1 - unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) *
          star (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G))) =
      1 - unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) *
        star (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G))
    calc
      ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint
          (1 - unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) *
          star (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G))) =
          ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (1 : lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 →L[𝕜]
            lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2) -
            ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint
              (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) *
                star (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G))) :=
        map_sub ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint _ _
      _ = 1 - ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint
          (star (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G))) ∘L
          ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint
            (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)) := by
        rw [ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_one, ContinuousLinearMap.mul_def,
          ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_comp]
      _ = 1 - unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) *
          star (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)) := by
        rw [ContinuousLinearMap.star_eq_adjoint,
          ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_adjoint, ContinuousLinearMap.mul_def]

private theorem unilateralShiftDefectProjection_eq_single_comp_eval :
    unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) =
      (lp.singleContinuousLinearMap 𝕜 (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 0).comp
        (lp.evalCLM 𝕜 (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 0) := by
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
  intro x
  apply lp.ext
  funext n
  cases n with
  | zero =>
      rw [unilateralShiftDefectProjection_apply_zero, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply,
        lp.singleContinuousLinearMap_apply, lp.single_apply_self]
      rfl
  | succ n =>
      rw [unilateralShiftDefectProjection_apply_succ, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply,
        lp.singleContinuousLinearMap_apply]
      rw [lp.single_apply_ne (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 0
        ((lp.evalCLM 𝕜 (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 0) x)
        (Nat.succ_ne_zero n)]

/-- The defect projection is compact when the multiplicity space is finite-dimensional. -/
theorem unilateralShiftDefectProjection_isCompact [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 G] :
    IsCompactOperator
      (unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)) := by
  let _ : ProperSpace G := FiniteDimensional.proper_rclike 𝕜 G
  rw [unilateralShiftDefectProjection_eq_single_comp_eval]
  exact (isCompactOperator_of_locallyCompactSpace_rng
    (lp.singleContinuousLinearMap 𝕜 (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 0)).comp_clm _

/-- Star-multiplication form of the unilateral shift's isometry equation. -/
@[simp]
theorem star_unilateralShift_mul_unilateralShift :
    star (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)) *
      unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) = 1 := by
  rw [ContinuousLinearMap.star_eq_adjoint, ContinuousLinearMap.mul_def]
  exact backwardShift_comp_unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)

/-- Star-multiplication form of the unilateral shift's defect equation. -/
theorem unilateralShift_mul_star_unilateralShift :
    unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) *
      star (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)) =
        1 - unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G) := by
  rw [ContinuousLinearMap.star_eq_adjoint, ContinuousLinearMap.mul_def]
  exact unilateralShift_comp_backwardShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)

omit hG in
private theorem unilateralShift_evalZero_surjective :
    Function.Surjective
      (lp.evalCLM 𝕜 (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 0) := by
  intro g
  refine ⟨lp.single (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 0 g, ?_⟩
  change lp.single (E := fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 0 g 0 = g
  rw [lp.single_apply_self]

private theorem unilateralShift_range_eq_ker_evalZero :
    (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)).range =
      (lp.evalCLM 𝕜 (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 0).ker := by
  rw [← unilateralShiftDefectProjection_ker (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)]
  ext x
  constructor
  · intro hx
    change unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) x = 0 at hx
    change x 0 = 0
    simpa using congrArg (fun y => y 0) hx
  · intro hx
    change x 0 = 0 at hx
    change unilateralShiftDefectProjection (𝕜 := 𝕜) x = 0
    apply lp.ext
    funext n
    cases n with
    | zero => simp [hx]
    | succ n => simp

private noncomputable def unilateralShiftCokerEquiv :
    (lp (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 ⧸
      (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)).range) ≃ₗ[𝕜] G :=
  (Submodule.quotEquivOfEq _ _
      (unilateralShift_range_eq_ker_evalZero (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G))).trans
    ((lp.evalCLM 𝕜 (fun _ : ℕ ↦ G) 2 0).toLinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective
      (unilateralShift_evalZero_surjective (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)))

/-- The unilateral shift is Fredholm exactly when its multiplicity space is finite-dimensional. -/
theorem unilateralShift_isFredholm_iff :
    (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)).IsFredholm ↔
      FiniteDimensional 𝕜 G := by
  constructor
  · intro hS
    let _ : (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)).range.CoFG :=
      hS.finite_coker
    let e := unilateralShiftCokerEquiv (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)
    exact FiniteDimensional.of_injective e.symm.toLinearMap e.symm.injective
  · intro hG
    let _ : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 G := hG
    let e := unilateralShiftCokerEquiv (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)
    have hcofg : (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)).range.CoFG :=
      FiniteDimensional.of_injective e.toLinearMap e.injective
    exact (unilateralShift_isometry (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)).isClosedEmbedding.isFredholm hcofg

/-- The algebraic index of the unilateral shift is minus the finite rank of its
multiplicity space. For infinite-dimensional multiplicity, both totalized
finite-rank expressions are zero; this does not assert Fredholmness. -/
theorem unilateralShift_index :
    (unilateralShift (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)).index =
      -(Module.finrank 𝕜 G : ℤ) := by
  rw [LinearMap.index_of_injective
    (unilateralShift_injective (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G))]
  rw [(unilateralShiftCokerEquiv (𝕜 := 𝕜) (G := G)).finrank_eq]

end lp

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Basic
public import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Module.Star
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Bilinear
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.DoubleDual

/-!
# Original continuous-dual involution and its isometry

The intrinsic dual involution is `phi*(a) = star (phi (star a))` on the
original continuous dual, with its original operator norm. It is linear
in the coefficient and conjugate-linear in the functional. The same
construction on the actual first dual gives the double-dual involution.

The dual star instances are scoped to `StrongDual`; activate them with
`open scoped StrongDual`. The named isometry remains directly usable.

Only the original isometric additive involution and compatible scalar
star are used. Coefficients may be seminormed, incomplete and zero;
no coefficient multiplication, unit, C-star identity or predual model is
required for this primitive construction.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

noncomputable section

universe u v

namespace StrongDual

variable {𝕜 : Type u} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [StarRing 𝕜] [NormedStarGroup 𝕜]
variable {A : Type v} [SeminormedAddCommGroup A] [StarAddMonoid A]
variable [NormedSpace 𝕜 A] [StarModule 𝕜 A] [NormedStarGroup A]

/-- The actual conjugate-linear dual isometry, formed from the original
coefficient and scalar continuous star equivalences. -/
def intrinsicStarIsometry : StrongDual 𝕜 A ≃ₗᵢ⋆[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 A := by
  let e : StrongDual 𝕜 A ≃ₗ⋆[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 A :=
    ContinuousLinearEquiv.arrowCongrEquivₛₗ
      (starL 𝕜 : A ≃L⋆[𝕜] A) (starL 𝕜 : 𝕜 ≃L⋆[𝕜] 𝕜)
  have hval : ∀ (phi : StrongDual 𝕜 A) (a : A), e phi a = star (phi (star a)) :=
    fun _ _ => rfl
  have hinv : ∀ phi : StrongDual 𝕜 A, e (e phi) = phi := by
    intro phi
    ext a
    simp only [hval, star_star]
  have hbound : ∀ phi : StrongDual 𝕜 A, ‖e phi‖ ≤ ‖phi‖ := by
    intro phi
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound (e phi) (norm_nonneg phi)
    intro a
    simpa only [hval, norm_star] using phi.le_opNorm (star a)
  refine { toLinearEquiv := e, norm_map' := ?_ }
  intro phi
  exact le_antisymm (hbound phi) (by simpa only [hinv] using hbound (e phi))

/-- The intrinsic star on the original continuous dual; it is not an operator
adjoint on an arbitrarily chosen Hilbert representation. -/
scoped instance intrinsicStar : Star (StrongDual 𝕜 A) where
  star phi := intrinsicStarIsometry phi

/-- Literal evaluation of the original dual involution. -/
@[simp] theorem star_apply (phi : StrongDual 𝕜 A) (a : A) :
    star phi a = star (phi (star a)) := rfl

/-- The dual involution squares to the identity on every actual functional. -/
scoped instance intrinsicInvolutiveStar : InvolutiveStar (StrongDual 𝕜 A) where
  star_involutive phi := by
    ext a
    simp only [star_apply, star_star]

/-- The dual star preserves the original additive structure. -/
scoped instance intrinsicStarAddMonoid : StarAddMonoid (StrongDual 𝕜 A) where
  star_add phi psi := (intrinsicStarIsometry (𝕜 := 𝕜) (A := A)).map_add phi psi

/-- Conjugate scalar linearity on the original dual functional space. -/
scoped instance intrinsicStarModule : StarModule 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A) where
  star_smul c phi := (intrinsicStarIsometry (𝕜 := 𝕜) (A := A)).map_smulₛₗ c phi

/-- The dual involution preserves the original operator norm. -/
scoped instance intrinsicNormedStarGroup : NormedStarGroup (StrongDual 𝕜 A) where
  norm_star_le phi := ((intrinsicStarIsometry (𝕜 := 𝕜) (A := A)).norm_map phi).le

/-- The constructed conjugate-linear isometry is precisely the dual star. -/
theorem intrinsicStarIsometry_apply (phi : StrongDual 𝕜 A) :
    intrinsicStarIsometry phi = star phi := rfl

/-- The actual dual involution is an isometry in the original operator metric. -/
theorem intrinsicStar_isometry : Isometry (star : StrongDual 𝕜 A → StrongDual 𝕜 A) :=
  (intrinsicStarIsometry (𝕜 := 𝕜) (A := A)).isometry

/-- The literal double-dual evaluation uses the actual original first-dual star. -/
theorem star_bidual_apply (p : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) (phi : StrongDual 𝕜 A) :
    star p phi = star (p (star phi)) := star_apply p phi

/-- The original evaluation embedding commutes with the coefficient involution. -/
@[simp] theorem star_inclusionInDoubleDual (a : A) :
    star (NormedSpace.inclusionInDoubleDual 𝕜 A a) =
      NormedSpace.inclusionInDoubleDual 𝕜 A (star a) := by
  ext phi
  change star (star phi a) = phi (star a)
  simp only [star_apply, star_star]

end StrongDual

Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Basic
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Dimension.LinearMap
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Dimension.Finite
public import Mathlib.Order.ConditionallyCompleteLattice.Basic
public import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith

/-!
# Approximation numbers for native continuous linear operators

The approximation number at index `n` is the infimum of `‖T-R‖` over
continuous linear operators whose range has cardinal rank at most `n`.
No finite-dimensional assumption on either carrier is made.

The indexing begins with `a₀(T)=‖T‖`. Classical approximation numbers
defined using rank strictly less than a positive index `k` correspond to
this definition at `k-1`.

This supplies the infinite-dimensional continuous-linear-map surface left
as a TODO in Mathlib's finite-dimensional singular-values API. Cardinal
rank is used because `finrank` alone is zero for infinite-dimensional
ranges and cannot express the finite-rank constraint.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

universe u v

namespace ContinuousLinearMap

variable {𝕜 : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
variable {E : Type u} {F : Type v}
variable [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedAddCommGroup F]
variable [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]

/-- Operator-norm errors of all approximants with actual cardinal range rank at most `n`. -/
def approximationErrorSet (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ) : Set ℝ :=
  {r | ∃ R : E →L[𝕜] F, R.toLinearMap.rank ≤ (n : Cardinal) ∧ r = ‖T - R‖}

/-- Membership records the actual finite-rank operator and its operator-norm error. -/
@[simp] theorem mem_approximationErrorSet (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ) (r : ℝ) :
    r ∈ approximationErrorSet T n ↔
      ∃ R : E →L[𝕜] F, R.toLinearMap.rank ≤ (n : Cardinal) ∧ r = ‖T - R‖ := Iff.rfl

/-- The zero approximant always gives the original operator norm as an admissible error. -/
theorem norm_mem_approximationErrorSet (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ) :
    ‖T‖ ∈ approximationErrorSet T n := by
  refine ⟨0, ?_, by simp⟩
  simp

/-- Finite-rank approximation errors form a nonempty set. -/
theorem approximationErrorSet_nonempty (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ) :
    (approximationErrorSet T n).Nonempty :=
  ⟨‖T‖, norm_mem_approximationErrorSet T n⟩

/-- Every actual approximation error is nonnegative. -/
theorem approximationErrorSet_nonneg (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ)
    {r : ℝ} (h : r ∈ approximationErrorSet T n) : 0 ≤ r := by
  obtain ⟨R, _, rfl⟩ := h
  exact norm_nonneg _

/-- The error set is bounded below by zero before taking the real infimum. -/
theorem approximationErrorSet_bddBelow (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ) :
    BddBelow (approximationErrorSet T n) :=
  ⟨0, fun _ h => approximationErrorSet_nonneg T n h⟩

/-- The approximation number at index `n`, using rank at most `n` and the real operator norm. -/
def approximationNumber (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sInf (approximationErrorSet T n)

/-- Approximation numbers are nonnegative. -/
theorem approximationNumber_nonneg (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ) :
    0 ≤ approximationNumber T n :=
  le_csInf (approximationErrorSet_nonempty T n) (fun _ h => approximationErrorSet_nonneg T n h)

/-- The zero approximant bounds every approximation number by the operator norm. -/
theorem approximationNumber_le_norm (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ) :
    approximationNumber T n ≤ ‖T‖ :=
  csInf_le (approximationErrorSet_bddBelow T n) (norm_mem_approximationErrorSet T n)

/-- Any admissible finite-rank operator bounds the approximation number by its actual error. -/
theorem approximationNumber_le_norm_sub (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ)
    (R : E →L[𝕜] F) (hR : R.toLinearMap.rank ≤ (n : Cardinal)) :
    approximationNumber T n ≤ ‖T - R‖ :=
  csInf_le (approximationErrorSet_bddBelow T n) ⟨R, hR, rfl⟩

/-- Enlarging the permitted rank enlarges the set of admissible errors. -/
theorem approximationErrorSet_mono (T : E →L[𝕜] F) {n m : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) :
    approximationErrorSet T n ⊆ approximationErrorSet T m := by
  rintro r ⟨R, hR, hr⟩
  exact ⟨R, hR.trans (Nat.cast_le.mpr h), hr⟩

/-- Approximation numbers decrease when more finite-rank approximants are allowed. -/
theorem approximationNumber_antitone (T : E →L[𝕜] F) : Antitone (approximationNumber T) := by
  intro n m h
  apply le_csInf (approximationErrorSet_nonempty T n)
  intro r hr
  exact csInf_le (approximationErrorSet_bddBelow T m) (approximationErrorSet_mono T h hr)

/-- Cardinal range rank zero forces the actual operator to be zero. -/
private theorem eq_zero_of_rank_le_zero (R : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (hR : R.toLinearMap.rank ≤ (0 : Cardinal)) : R = 0 := by
  have hbot : LinearMap.range R.toLinearMap = ⊥ :=
    Submodule.rank_eq_zero.mp (le_antisymm hR (zero_le : (0 : Cardinal) ≤ R.toLinearMap.rank))
  have hlinear : R.toLinearMap = 0 := LinearMap.range_eq_bot.mp hbot
  ext x
  simpa using LinearMap.congr_fun hlinear x

/-- Index zero permits only the zero operator, so its approximation number is the operator norm. -/
@[simp] theorem approximationNumber_zero_index (T : E →L[𝕜] F) :
    approximationNumber T 0 = ‖T‖ := by
  apply le_antisymm (approximationNumber_le_norm T 0)
  apply le_csInf (approximationErrorSet_nonempty T 0)
  rintro r ⟨R, hR, rfl⟩
  rw [eq_zero_of_rank_le_zero R hR, sub_zero]

/-- An operator with cardinal range rank at most `n` has zero approximation error at that index. -/
theorem approximationNumber_eq_zero_of_rank_le (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ)
    (hT : T.toLinearMap.rank ≤ (n : Cardinal)) : approximationNumber T n = 0 := by
  apply le_antisymm _ (approximationNumber_nonneg T n)
  simpa using approximationNumber_le_norm_sub T n T hT

/-- Every approximation number of the zero operator is zero. -/
@[simp] theorem approximationNumber_zero (n : ℕ) :
    approximationNumber (0 : E →L[𝕜] F) n = 0 := by
  apply approximationNumber_eq_zero_of_rank_le
  simp

/-- A common finite-rank approximant gives the one-sided operator-norm stability inequality. -/
theorem approximationNumber_le_add_norm_sub (T S : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ) :
    approximationNumber T n ≤ approximationNumber S n + ‖T - S‖ := by
  have h : approximationNumber T n - ‖T - S‖ ≤ approximationNumber S n := by
    apply le_csInf (approximationErrorSet_nonempty S n)
    rintro r ⟨R, hR, rfl⟩
    have h₁ := approximationNumber_le_norm_sub T n R hR
    have h₂ := dist_triangle T S R
    simp only [dist_eq_norm] at h₂
    linarith
  linarith

/-- Approximation numbers are 1-Lipschitz in the native operator norm. -/
theorem abs_approximationNumber_sub_le_norm (T S : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ) :
    |approximationNumber T n - approximationNumber S n| ≤ ‖T - S‖ := by
  have h₁ := approximationNumber_le_add_norm_sub T S n
  have h₂ := approximationNumber_le_add_norm_sub S T n
  rw [norm_sub_rev S T] at h₂
  exact abs_le.mpr ⟨by linarith, by linarith⟩

end ContinuousLinearMap
