Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Operator.ApproximationNumbers
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Field.Basic
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Dimension.DivisionRing

/-!
# Operator ideal laws for approximation numbers

Finite-rank approximants remain admissible under composition. The proofs use
cardinal range rank and infimum lower bounds, without assuming a minimizing
approximant or finite-dimensional carriers. Indices retain the rank-at-most
convention of `approximationNumber`.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

universe u v w z

namespace ContinuousLinearMap

variable {𝕜 : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
variable {D : Type u} {E : Type v} {F : Type w} {G : Type z}
variable [NormedAddCommGroup D] [NormedAddCommGroup E]
variable [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedAddCommGroup G]
variable [NormedSpace 𝕜 D] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
variable [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 G]

private theorem rank_precomp_budget (R : E →L[𝕜] F) (A : D →L[𝕜] E)
    {n : ℕ} (hR : R.toLinearMap.rank ≤ (n : Cardinal)) :
    (R.comp A).toLinearMap.rank ≤ (n : Cardinal) := by
  exact (LinearMap.rank_comp_le_left A.toLinearMap R.toLinearMap).trans hR

private theorem rank_postcomp_budget (R : E →L[𝕜] F) (B : F →L[𝕜] G)
    {n : ℕ} (hR : R.toLinearMap.rank ≤ (n : Cardinal)) :
    (B.comp R).toLinearMap.rank ≤ (n : Cardinal) := by
  have h := (LinearMap.lift_rank_comp_le_right R.toLinearMap B.toLinearMap).trans
    (Cardinal.lift_le.mpr hR)
  have h' : Cardinal.lift.{w} ((B.comp R).toLinearMap.rank) ≤
      Cardinal.lift.{w} (n : Cardinal.{z}) := by
    simpa only [Cardinal.lift_natCast, toLinearMap_comp] using h
  exact Cardinal.lift_le.mp h'

private theorem le_mul_approximationNumber_of_le_errors (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ)
    (a c : ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ c)
    (h : ∀ R : E →L[𝕜] F, R.toLinearMap.rank ≤ (n : Cardinal) → a ≤ c * ‖T - R‖) :
    a ≤ c * approximationNumber T n := by
  by_cases hzero : c = 0
  · subst c
    simpa using h 0 (by simp)
  · have hpos : 0 < c := lt_of_le_of_ne hc (Ne.symm hzero)
    have hbound : a / c ≤ approximationNumber T n := by
      apply le_csInf (approximationErrorSet_nonempty T n)
      rintro r ⟨R, hR, rfl⟩
      exact (div_le_iff₀ hpos).mpr (by simpa only [mul_comm] using h R hR)
    simpa only [mul_comm] using (div_le_iff₀ hpos).mp hbound

/-- Approximation numbers satisfy the two-sided operator ideal norm inequality. -/
theorem approximationNumber_comp_le (B : F →L[𝕜] G) (T : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (A : D →L[𝕜] E) (n : ℕ) :
    approximationNumber (B.comp (T.comp A)) n ≤ ‖B‖ * approximationNumber T n * ‖A‖ := by
  have hbound : approximationNumber (B.comp (T.comp A)) n ≤
      (‖B‖ * ‖A‖) * approximationNumber T n := by
    apply le_mul_approximationNumber_of_le_errors T n _ _
      (mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg B) (norm_nonneg A))
    intro R hR
    have hRank := rank_postcomp_budget (R.comp A) B (rank_precomp_budget R A hR)
    calc
      _ ≤ ‖B.comp (T.comp A) - B.comp (R.comp A)‖ :=
        approximationNumber_le_norm_sub _ n _ hRank
      _ = ‖B.comp ((T - R).comp A)‖ := by rw [sub_comp, comp_sub]
      _ ≤ ‖B‖ * ‖(T - R).comp A‖ := opNorm_comp_le _ _
      _ ≤ ‖B‖ * (‖T - R‖ * ‖A‖) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (opNorm_comp_le _ _) (norm_nonneg B)
      _ = (‖B‖ * ‖A‖) * ‖T - R‖ := by ac_rfl
  simpa only [mul_assoc, mul_comm, mul_left_comm] using hbound

private theorem approximationNumber_smul_le (c : 𝕜) (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ) :
    approximationNumber (c • T) n ≤ ‖c‖ * approximationNumber T n := by
  apply le_mul_approximationNumber_of_le_errors T n _ _ (norm_nonneg c)
  intro R hR
  have hRank : (c • R).toLinearMap.rank ≤ (n : Cardinal) := by
    simpa only [smul_comp, id_comp] using
      rank_postcomp_budget R (c • ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 F) hR
  have h := approximationNumber_le_norm_sub (c • T) n (c • R) hRank
  simpa only [← smul_sub, norm_smul] using h

/-- Scalar multiplication scales approximation numbers by the scalar norm. -/
@[simp] theorem approximationNumber_smul (c : 𝕜) (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ) :
    approximationNumber (c • T) n = ‖c‖ * approximationNumber T n := by
  apply le_antisymm (approximationNumber_smul_le c T n)
  by_cases hc : c = 0
  · subst c
    simp
  · have h := approximationNumber_smul_le c⁻¹ (c • T) n
    have hcancel : c⁻¹ • (c • T) = T := by
      rw [smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀ hc, one_smul]
    rw [hcancel, norm_inv] at h
    have hnorm : ‖c‖ ≠ 0 := norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr hc
    have h' := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h (norm_nonneg c)
    simpa only [← mul_assoc, mul_inv_cancel₀ hnorm, one_mul] using h'

private theorem rank_add_budget (R S : E →L[𝕜] F) {n m : ℕ}
    (hR : R.toLinearMap.rank ≤ (n : Cardinal))
    (hS : S.toLinearMap.rank ≤ (m : Cardinal)) :
    (R + S).toLinearMap.rank ≤ ((n + m : ℕ) : Cardinal) := by
  calc
    _ ≤ R.toLinearMap.rank + S.toLinearMap.rank := LinearMap.rank_add_le _ _
    _ ≤ (n : Cardinal) + (m : Cardinal) := add_le_add hR hS
    _ = ((n + m : ℕ) : Cardinal) := (Nat.cast_add n m).symm

/-- Adding two operators adds their finite-rank approximation budgets. -/
theorem approximationNumber_add_le (T S : E →L[𝕜] F) (n m : ℕ) :
    approximationNumber (T + S) (n + m) ≤ approximationNumber T n + approximationNumber S m := by
  have hbound : approximationNumber (T + S) (n + m) - approximationNumber T n ≤
      approximationNumber S m := by
    apply le_csInf (approximationErrorSet_nonempty S m)
    rintro r ⟨R₂, hR₂, rfl⟩
    have hinner : approximationNumber (T + S) (n + m) - ‖S - R₂‖ ≤
        approximationNumber T n := by
      apply le_csInf (approximationErrorSet_nonempty T n)
      rintro r ⟨R₁, hR₁, rfl⟩
      have ha := approximationNumber_le_norm_sub (T + S) (n + m) (R₁ + R₂)
        (rank_add_budget R₁ R₂ hR₁ hR₂)
      have hn : ‖T + S - (R₁ + R₂)‖ ≤ ‖T - R₁‖ + ‖S - R₂‖ := by
        rw [add_sub_add_comm]
        exact norm_add_le _ _
      linarith
    linarith
  linarith

end ContinuousLinearMap

/-
Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Bilinear
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.DoubleDual

/-!
# Bounded dual transposes and the two Arens extensions

For an actual continuous bilinear map `m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G`, bounded
precomposition gives `(phi, x, y) ↦ phi (m x y)`. Three successive dual
transposes define its first Arens extension on the original strong biduals.
Flipping the original map and the resulting extension gives the second.

The dual norms, evaluations and named weak-star views are Mathlib's existing
ones. In particular, multiplication in a nonunital normed algebra supplies
`m` directly through `ContinuousLinearMap.mul`. The two extensions retain
the original order of the coefficient multiplication. Associativity, Arens
regularity, involution, a unit and a C-star identity are later prerequisites.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

noncomputable section

universe u v w z

namespace ContinuousLinearMap

variable {𝕜 : Type u} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
variable {E : Type v} {F : Type w} {G : Type z}
variable [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
variable [SeminormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]
variable [SeminormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace 𝕜 G]

/- The literal local declarations preserve the exact imported stock
instance setup at every iterated transpose level. Their variables are
polymorphic, so the same rules cover later strong-dual and dual-target levels. -/

/-- The original operator seminorm structure on an actual continuous dual. -/
local instance arensDualSeminormed : SeminormedAddCommGroup (StrongDual 𝕜 G) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.toSeminormedAddCommGroup

/-- The existing scalar action and norm bound on that same continuous dual. -/
local instance arensDualNormedSpace : NormedSpace 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 G) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.toNormedSpace

/-- The original operator seminorm on maps into an actual continuous dual. -/
local instance arensDualTargetSeminormed : SeminormedAddCommGroup (E →L[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 F) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.toSeminormedAddCommGroup

/-- The existing normed scalar action on those actual dual-target maps. -/
local instance arensDualTargetNormedSpace : NormedSpace 𝕜 (E →L[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 F) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.toNormedSpace

/-- Continuity of addition for the same inherited operator topology. -/
local instance arensDualTargetTopologicalAddGroup : IsTopologicalAddGroup (E →L[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 F) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.isTopologicalAddGroup

/-- The original operator seminorm on the ordinary maps used by composition. -/
local instance arensMapSeminormed : SeminormedAddCommGroup (F →L[𝕜] G) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.toSeminormedAddCommGroup

/-- The existing scalar action on those original ordinary maps. -/
local instance arensMapNormedSpace : NormedSpace 𝕜 (F →L[𝕜] G) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.toNormedSpace

/-- Addition is continuous for the original ordinary operator topology. -/
local instance arensMapTopologicalAddGroup : IsTopologicalAddGroup (F →L[𝕜] G) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.isTopologicalAddGroup

/-- The original iterated operator seminorm on the actual second dual. -/
local instance arensBidualSeminormed : SeminormedAddCommGroup (StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E)) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.toSeminormedAddCommGroup

/-- The stock scalar action on the original second dual and its unchanged norm. -/
local instance arensBidualNormedSpace : NormedSpace 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E)) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.toNormedSpace

/-- The original operator seminorm on maps between the actual second duals. -/
local instance arensBidualMapSeminormed : SeminormedAddCommGroup
    (StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F) →L[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 G)) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.toSeminormedAddCommGroup

/-- The existing scalar action on those second-dual operator maps. -/
local instance arensBidualMapNormedSpace : NormedSpace 𝕜
    (StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F) →L[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 G)) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.toNormedSpace

/-- Continuity of addition for the original second-dual operator topology. -/
local instance arensBidualMapTopologicalAddGroup : IsTopologicalAddGroup
    (StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F) →L[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 G)) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.isTopologicalAddGroup

/-- Bounded dual precomposition with the literal formula `phi (m x y)`.
The three coefficient-space universes are independent, and zero spaces are allowed. -/
noncomputable def dualBilinear (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G) :
    StrongDual 𝕜 G →L[𝕜] E →L[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 F :=
  ((compL 𝕜 F G 𝕜).flip.comp m).flip

/-- Evaluation of the bounded dual transpose uses the original bilinear value. -/
@[simp] theorem dualBilinear_apply (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G)
    (phi : StrongDual 𝕜 G) (x : E) (y : F) :
    m.dualBilinear phi x y = phi (m x y) := rfl

/-- Dual precomposition does not increase the original bilinear operator norm. -/
theorem norm_dualBilinear_le (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G) :
    ‖m.dualBilinear‖ ≤ ‖m‖ := by
  calc
    ‖m.dualBilinear‖ = ‖(compL 𝕜 F G 𝕜).flip.comp m‖ :=
      opNorm_flip ((compL 𝕜 F G 𝕜).flip.comp m)
    _ ≤ ‖(compL 𝕜 F G 𝕜).flip‖ * ‖m‖ := opNorm_comp_le (compL 𝕜 F G 𝕜).flip m
    _ = ‖compL 𝕜 F G 𝕜‖ * ‖m‖ := by rw [opNorm_flip]
    _ ≤ 1 * ‖m‖ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (norm_compL_le 𝕜 F G 𝕜) (norm_nonneg m)
    _ = ‖m‖ := one_mul _

/-- The actual transposed functional has the product bound in the original dual norm. -/
theorem norm_dualBilinear_apply_le (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G)
    (phi : StrongDual 𝕜 G) (x : E) :
    ‖m.dualBilinear phi x‖ ≤ ‖m‖ * ‖phi‖ * ‖x‖ := by
  exact (m.dualBilinear.le_opNorm₂ phi x).trans <| by
    gcongr
    exact norm_dualBilinear_le m

/-- The first Arens extension on the original iterated continuous duals.
Its outer evaluation is by the first bidual variable. -/
noncomputable def arensFirst (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G) :
    StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E) →L[𝕜]
      StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F) →L[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 G) :=
  m.dualBilinear.dualBilinear.dualBilinear

/-- The second Arens extension preserves the original bilinear order while
putting the second bidual variable in the outer evaluation. -/
noncomputable def arensSecond (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G) :
    StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E) →L[𝕜]
      StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F) →L[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 G) :=
  m.flip.arensFirst.flip

/-- The literal first Arens evaluation, using an actual bounded iterated dual action. -/
@[simp] theorem arensFirst_apply (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G)
    (p : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E))
    (q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F)) (phi : StrongDual 𝕜 G) :
    m.arensFirst p q phi = p (m.dualBilinear.dualBilinear q phi) := rfl

/-- The literal second Arens evaluation, with the same original multiplication order. -/
@[simp] theorem arensSecond_apply (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G)
    (p : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E))
    (q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F)) (phi : StrongDual 𝕜 G) :
    m.arensSecond p q phi = q (m.flip.dualBilinear.dualBilinear p phi) := rfl

/-- The first Arens bilinear map is bounded by the norm of the original map. -/
theorem norm_arensFirst_le (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G) : ‖m.arensFirst‖ ≤ ‖m‖ :=
  (norm_dualBilinear_le m.dualBilinear.dualBilinear).trans
    ((norm_dualBilinear_le m.dualBilinear).trans (norm_dualBilinear_le m))

/-- The second Arens bilinear map has the same original operator norm bound. -/
theorem norm_arensSecond_le (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G) : ‖m.arensSecond‖ ≤ ‖m‖ := by
  calc
    ‖m.arensSecond‖ = ‖m.flip.arensFirst‖ := opNorm_flip m.flip.arensFirst
    _ ≤ ‖m.flip‖ := norm_arensFirst_le m.flip
    _ = ‖m‖ := opNorm_flip m

/-- The first Arens value has its original iterated-dual product norm bound. -/
theorem norm_arensFirst_apply_le (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G)
    (p : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E))
    (q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F)) :
    ‖m.arensFirst p q‖ ≤ ‖m‖ * ‖p‖ * ‖q‖ := by
  exact (m.arensFirst.le_opNorm₂ p q).trans <| by
    gcongr
    exact norm_arensFirst_le m

/-- The second Arens value has the analogous bound in the unchanged dual norm. -/
theorem norm_arensSecond_apply_le (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G)
    (p : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E))
    (q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F)) :
    ‖m.arensSecond p q‖ ≤ ‖m‖ * ‖p‖ * ‖q‖ := by
  exact (m.arensSecond.le_opNorm₂ p q).trans <| by
    gcongr
    exact norm_arensSecond_le m

/-- The first extension preserves the actual original evaluation embedding. -/
@[simp] theorem arensFirst_inclusion (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G) (x : E) (y : F) :
    m.arensFirst (NormedSpace.inclusionInDoubleDual 𝕜 E x)
      (NormedSpace.inclusionInDoubleDual 𝕜 F y) =
        NormedSpace.inclusionInDoubleDual 𝕜 G (m x y) := by
  ext phi
  rfl

/-- The second extension also preserves that same original evaluation embedding. -/
@[simp] theorem arensSecond_inclusion (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G) (x : E) (y : F) :
    m.arensSecond (NormedSpace.inclusionInDoubleDual 𝕜 E x)
      (NormedSpace.inclusionInDoubleDual 𝕜 F y) =
        NormedSpace.inclusionInDoubleDual 𝕜 G (m x y) := by
  ext phi
  rfl

/-- The first Arens product is weak-star continuous in its first variable,
using precisely the original first duals as the fixed pairing spaces. -/
theorem continuous_arensFirst_weakDual_left (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G)
    (q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F)) :
    Continuous (fun p : WeakDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E) =>
      StrongDual.toWeakDual (m.arensFirst p.toStrongDual q)) := by
  apply WeakDual.continuous_of_continuous_eval
  intro phi
  change Continuous (fun p : WeakDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E) =>
    p (m.dualBilinear.dualBilinear q phi))
  exact WeakDual.eval_continuous _

/-- The second Arens product is weak-star continuous in its second variable,
with the same named original-dual pairing and unchanged product values. -/
theorem continuous_arensSecond_weakDual_right (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G)
    (p : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E)) :
    Continuous (fun q : WeakDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F) =>
      StrongDual.toWeakDual (m.arensSecond p q.toStrongDual)) := by
  apply WeakDual.continuous_of_continuous_eval
  intro phi
  change Continuous (fun q : WeakDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F) =>
    q (m.flip.dualBilinear.dualBilinear p phi))
  exact WeakDual.eval_continuous _

end ContinuousLinearMap

module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Arens
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Mul
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.NormedSpace
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Completeness

/-!
# Associative Arens products and the original normed bidual ring

Associativity of an actual bounded coefficient multiplication implies
associativity of both Arens products on the original strong bidual. The
first product then gives that same carrier a nonunital normed ring, with
the original addition, distance and dual operator norm. Its scalar action
is the original continuous-dual action. Coefficients may be incomplete or
zero; only scalar completeness is used in the separately stated completeness
of the constructed bidual topology.

The committed Arens products and stock normed/group dictionaries are reused.
Involution, a unit, Arens regularity and the C-star identity remain separate
prerequisites.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

noncomputable section

universe u v

attribute [local instance]
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensDualSeminormed
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensDualNormedSpace
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensDualTargetSeminormed
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensDualTargetNormedSpace
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensDualTargetTopologicalAddGroup
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensMapSeminormed
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensMapNormedSpace
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensMapTopologicalAddGroup
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensBidualSeminormed
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensBidualNormedSpace
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensBidualMapSeminormed
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensBidualMapNormedSpace
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensBidualMapTopologicalAddGroup

namespace ContinuousLinearMap

variable {𝕜 : Type u} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
variable {A : Type v} [SeminormedAddCommGroup A] [NormedSpace 𝕜 A]

/-- The original dual operator seminorm separates continuous functionals,
even when the coefficient space itself is only seminormed. The standard
separation constructor retains exactly the original norm, distance and topology. -/
local instance arensAlgebraDualNormedGroup : NormedAddCommGroup (StrongDual 𝕜 A) :=
  NormedAddCommGroup.ofSeparation <| by
    intro phi hphi
    ext a
    apply norm_eq_zero.mp
    have hle : ‖phi a‖ ≤ 0 := by
      simpa only [hphi, zero_mul] using phi.le_opNorm a
    exact le_antisymm hle (norm_nonneg (phi a))

/-- The first Arens product is associative when the original bounded bilinear
multiplication is associative; the proof uses only the actual dual evaluations. -/
theorem arensFirst_assoc (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A)
    (h : ∀ a b c, m (m a b) c = m a (m b c))
    (p q r : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    m.arensFirst (m.arensFirst p q) r = m.arensFirst p (m.arensFirst q r) := by
  ext phi
  change p (m.dualBilinear.dualBilinear q (m.dualBilinear.dualBilinear r phi)) =
    p (m.dualBilinear.dualBilinear (m.arensFirst q r) phi)
  apply congrArg p
  ext a
  change q (m.dualBilinear (m.dualBilinear.dualBilinear r phi) a) =
    q (m.dualBilinear.dualBilinear r (m.dualBilinear phi a))
  apply congrArg q
  ext b
  change r (m.dualBilinear phi (m a b)) =
    r (m.dualBilinear (m.dualBilinear phi a) b)
  apply congrArg r
  ext c
  change phi (m (m a b) c) = phi (m a (m b c))
  exact congrArg phi (h a b c)

/-- The second Arens product is associative, with its original coefficient order. -/
theorem arensSecond_assoc (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A)
    (h : ∀ a b c, m (m a b) c = m a (m b c))
    (p q r : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    m.arensSecond (m.arensSecond p q) r = m.arensSecond p (m.arensSecond q r) := by
  have hflip : ∀ a b c, m.flip (m.flip a b) c = m.flip a (m.flip b c) := by
    intro a b c
    change m c (m b a) = m (m c b) a
    exact (h c b a).symm
  change m.flip.arensFirst r (m.flip.arensFirst q p) =
    m.flip.arensFirst (m.flip.arensFirst r q) p
  exact (arensFirst_assoc m.flip hflip r q p).symm

/-- Addition in the first variable distributes through the first Arens product. -/
theorem arensFirst_add_left (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A)
    (p q r : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    m.arensFirst (p + q) r = m.arensFirst p r + m.arensFirst q r :=
  congrArg (fun L : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A) →L[𝕜]
    StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A) => L r) (m.arensFirst.map_add p q)

/-- Addition in the second variable distributes through the first Arens product. -/
theorem arensFirst_add_right (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A)
    (p q r : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    m.arensFirst p (q + r) = m.arensFirst p q + m.arensFirst p r :=
  (m.arensFirst p).map_add q r

/-- Zero in the first variable gives the original zero bidual functional. -/
theorem arensFirst_zero_left (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A)
    (q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) : m.arensFirst 0 q = 0 := by
  ext phi
  rfl

/-- Zero in the second variable gives the same original zero functional. -/
theorem arensFirst_zero_right (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A)
    (p : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) : m.arensFirst p 0 = 0 :=
  (m.arensFirst p).map_zero

/-- Scalar multiplication in the first bidual variable commutes with its product. -/
theorem arensFirst_smul_left (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A) (c : 𝕜)
    (p q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    m.arensFirst (c • p) q = c • m.arensFirst p q :=
  congrArg (fun L : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A) →L[𝕜]
    StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A) => L q) (m.arensFirst.map_smul c p)

/-- Scalar multiplication in the second bidual variable commutes with its product. -/
theorem arensFirst_smul_right (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A) (c : 𝕜)
    (p q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    m.arensFirst p (c • q) = c • m.arensFirst p q :=
  (m.arensFirst p).map_smul c q

/-- Addition in the first variable distributes through the second Arens product. -/
theorem arensSecond_add_left (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A)
    (p q r : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    m.arensSecond (p + q) r = m.arensSecond p r + m.arensSecond q r :=
  congrArg (fun L : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A) →L[𝕜]
    StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A) => L r) (m.arensSecond.map_add p q)

/-- Addition in the second variable distributes through the second Arens product. -/
theorem arensSecond_add_right (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A)
    (p q r : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    m.arensSecond p (q + r) = m.arensSecond p q + m.arensSecond p r :=
  (m.arensSecond p).map_add q r

/-- The second product has zero value when its first input is zero. -/
theorem arensSecond_zero_left (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A)
    (q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) : m.arensSecond 0 q = 0 :=
  congrArg (fun L : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A) →L[𝕜]
    StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A) => L q) m.arensSecond.map_zero

/-- The second product has zero value when its second input is zero. -/
theorem arensSecond_zero_right (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A)
    (p : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) : m.arensSecond p 0 = 0 := by
  ext phi
  rfl

/-- The original scalar action is linear in the first variable of the second product. -/
theorem arensSecond_smul_left (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A) (c : 𝕜)
    (p q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    m.arensSecond (c • p) q = c • m.arensSecond p q :=
  congrArg (fun L : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A) →L[𝕜]
    StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A) => L q) (m.arensSecond.map_smul c p)

/-- The original scalar action is linear in the second variable of the second product. -/
theorem arensSecond_smul_right (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A) (c : 𝕜)
    (p q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    m.arensSecond p (c • q) = c • m.arensSecond p q :=
  (m.arensSecond p).map_smul c q

end ContinuousLinearMap

attribute [local instance] ContinuousLinearMap.arensAlgebraDualNormedGroup

namespace NormedSpace

variable (𝕜 : Type u) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
variable (A : Type v) [NonUnitalSeminormedRing A] [NormedSpace 𝕜 A]
variable [IsScalarTower 𝕜 A A] [SMulCommClass 𝕜 A A]

/-- The actual first Arens multiplication is bounded by the unchanged dual norms. -/
theorem firstArens_mul_norm_le (p q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    ‖(ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensFirst p q‖ ≤ ‖p‖ * ‖q‖ := by
  calc
    ‖(ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensFirst p q‖ ≤
        ‖ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A‖ * ‖p‖ * ‖q‖ :=
      (ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).norm_arensFirst_apply_le p q
    _ ≤ 1 * ‖p‖ * ‖q‖ := by
      gcongr
      exact ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_mul_le 𝕜 A
    _ = ‖p‖ * ‖q‖ := by rw [one_mul]

/-- The actual second Arens multiplication has the same original-norm bound. -/
theorem secondArens_mul_norm_le (p q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    ‖(ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensSecond p q‖ ≤ ‖p‖ * ‖q‖ := by
  calc
    ‖(ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensSecond p q‖ ≤
        ‖ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A‖ * ‖p‖ * ‖q‖ :=
      (ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).norm_arensSecond_apply_le p q
    _ ≤ 1 * ‖p‖ * ‖q‖ := by
      gcongr
      exact ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_mul_le 𝕜 A
    _ = ‖p‖ * ‖q‖ := by rw [one_mul]

/-- The first Arens product gives the literal original bidual a nonunital ring.
Addition and additive inverses are the pre-existing continuous-dual operations. -/
@[instance_reducible] noncomputable def firstArensNonUnitalRing :
    NonUnitalRing (StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) where
  __ := (inferInstance : AddCommGroup (StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)))
  mul := fun p q => (ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensFirst p q
  mul_assoc := fun p q r => (ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensFirst_assoc
    (fun a b c => mul_assoc a b c) p q r
  left_distrib := fun p q r => (ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensFirst_add_right p q r
  right_distrib := fun p q r => (ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensFirst_add_left p q r
  zero_mul := (ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensFirst_zero_left
  mul_zero := (ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensFirst_zero_right

/-- The actual nonunital ring and the original iterated dual metric/norm form
its normed ring dictionary; no norm is transported from another model. -/
@[instance_reducible] noncomputable def firstArensNonUnitalNormedRing :
    NonUnitalNormedRing (StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) where
  __ := firstArensNonUnitalRing 𝕜 A
  __ := (inferInstance : NormedAddCommGroup (StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)))
  dist_eq := fun p q => dist_eq_norm_neg_add p q
  norm_mul_le := firstArens_mul_norm_le 𝕜 A

/-- The constructed dictionary has precisely the original first Arens multiplication. -/
theorem firstArensNonUnitalNormedRing_mul
    (p q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    letI := firstArensNonUnitalNormedRing 𝕜 A
    p * q = (ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensFirst p q := rfl

/-- Its norm is definitionally the original strong-bidual operator norm. -/
theorem firstArensNonUnitalNormedRing_norm (p : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    (firstArensNonUnitalNormedRing 𝕜 A).toNorm.norm p = ‖p‖ := rfl

/-- Original scalar multiplication and the first Arens multiplication have the tower law. -/
theorem firstArensIsScalarTower :
    letI := firstArensNonUnitalNormedRing 𝕜 A
    IsScalarTower 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) (StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) := by
  let _ := firstArensNonUnitalNormedRing 𝕜 A
  refine ⟨?_⟩
  intro c p q
  exact (ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensFirst_smul_left c p q

/-- Scalar and left multiplication commute on the same actual first-Arens ring. -/
theorem firstArensSMulCommClass :
    letI := firstArensNonUnitalNormedRing 𝕜 A
    SMulCommClass 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) (StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) := by
  let _ := firstArensNonUnitalNormedRing 𝕜 A
  refine ⟨?_⟩
  intro c p q
  exact ((ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensFirst_smul_right c p q).symm

omit [IsScalarTower 𝕜 A A] [SMulCommClass 𝕜 A A] in
/-- With complete scalars, the constructed ring has the original complete dual topology.
No completeness hypothesis is imposed on the coefficient algebra A. -/
theorem firstArensCompleteSpace [CompleteSpace 𝕜] :
    CompleteSpace (StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) := by
  infer_instance

end NormedSpace

/-
Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Module.StrongDualStar
public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Operator.ArensAlgebra

/-!
# Involution interchanges the two original Arens products

The first product reverses into the second product under the original
dual involution. This uses only the original coefficient multiplication's
star-reversal law. No equality of the Arens products and no StarRing
structure on the first-Arens bidual is assumed or installed.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open scoped StrongDual

universe u v

attribute [local instance]
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensDualSeminormed
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensDualNormedSpace
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensDualTargetSeminormed
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensDualTargetNormedSpace
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensDualTargetTopologicalAddGroup
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensMapSeminormed
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensMapNormedSpace
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensMapTopologicalAddGroup
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensBidualSeminormed
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensBidualNormedSpace
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensBidualMapSeminormed
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensBidualMapNormedSpace
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensBidualMapTopologicalAddGroup
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensAlgebraDualNormedGroup

namespace ContinuousLinearMap

variable {𝕜 : Type u} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [StarRing 𝕜] [NormedStarGroup 𝕜]
variable {A : Type v} [SeminormedAddCommGroup A] [StarAddMonoid A]
variable [NormedSpace 𝕜 A] [StarModule 𝕜 A] [NormedStarGroup A]

/-- The original dual involution reverses the first Arens product into the second. -/
theorem arensFirst_star (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A)
    (h : ∀ a b, star (m a b) = m (star b) (star a))
    (p q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    star (m.arensFirst p q) = m.arensSecond (star q) (star p) := by
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
  intro phi
  change star (p (m.dualBilinear.dualBilinear q (star phi))) =
    star (p (star (m.flip.dualBilinear.dualBilinear (star q) phi)))
  apply congrArg (star : 𝕜 → 𝕜)
  apply congrArg (fun f : StrongDual 𝕜 A => p f)
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
  intro a
  change q (m.dualBilinear (star phi) a) =
    star (star q (m.flip.dualBilinear phi (star a)))
  rw [StrongDual.star_apply, star_star]
  apply congrArg (fun f : StrongDual 𝕜 A => q f)
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
  intro b
  change star (phi (star (m a b))) = star (phi (m (star b) (star a)))
  rw [h a b]

/-- The same involution reverses the second Arens product into the first. -/
theorem arensSecond_star (m : A →L[𝕜] A →L[𝕜] A)
    (h : ∀ a b, star (m a b) = m (star b) (star a))
    (p q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    star (m.arensSecond p q) = m.arensFirst (star q) (star p) := by
  have h' := congrArg star (arensFirst_star m h (star q) (star p))
  simpa only [star_star] using h'.symm

end ContinuousLinearMap

namespace NormedSpace

variable (𝕜 : Type u) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [StarRing 𝕜] [NormedStarGroup 𝕜]
variable (A : Type v) [NonUnitalSeminormedRing A] [StarRing A] [NormedStarGroup A]
variable [NormedSpace 𝕜 A] [StarModule 𝕜 A]
variable [IsScalarTower 𝕜 A A] [SMulCommClass 𝕜 A A]

/-- Original nonunital star multiplication gives the exact first-to-second reversal. -/
theorem firstArens_star_mul (p q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    star ((ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensFirst p q) =
      (ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensSecond (star q) (star p) :=
  (ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensFirst_star (fun a b => star_mul a b) p q

/-- Original nonunital star multiplication gives the exact second-to-first reversal. -/
theorem secondArens_star_mul (p q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 A)) :
    star ((ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensSecond p q) =
      (ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensFirst (star q) (star p) :=
  (ContinuousLinearMap.mul 𝕜 A).arensSecond_star (fun a b => star_mul a b) p q

end NormedSpace

Author: @toskua

module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Operator.ArensStar

/-!
# Original Arens maps and involution in the fixed weak-star views

The first Arens extension with its second variable fixed is a continuous
linear map on the original first weak-star bidual. The second extension
with its first variable fixed has the corresponding continuous linear map
on the second weak-star bidual. Their values are the existing extensions.

The original dual involution is a conjugate-linear continuous equivalence
on the weak-star view paired with the same coefficient space. Changing
views preserves its values and the original continuous-dual norm.

These data require only the original bounded bilinear map and isometric
additive involution. No equality of the Arens products, C-star identity,
unit, selected predual or representation model is used.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open scoped StrongDual

universe u v w z

attribute [local instance]
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensDualSeminormed
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensDualNormedSpace
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensDualTargetSeminormed
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensDualTargetNormedSpace
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensDualTargetTopologicalAddGroup
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensMapSeminormed
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensMapNormedSpace
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensMapTopologicalAddGroup
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensBidualSeminormed
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensBidualNormedSpace
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensBidualMapSeminormed
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensBidualMapNormedSpace
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensBidualMapTopologicalAddGroup
  ContinuousLinearMap.arensAlgebraDualNormedGroup

namespace ContinuousLinearMap

variable {𝕜 : Type u} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
variable {E : Type v} {F : Type w} {G : Type z}
variable [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
variable [SeminormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]
variable [SeminormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace 𝕜 G]

/-- The actual first Arens extension in its continuous first weak-star variable. -/
def arensFirstWeakLeft (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G)
    (q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F)) :
    WeakDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E) →L[𝕜] WeakDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 G) where
  toLinearMap :=
    (StrongDual.toWeakDual (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := StrongDual 𝕜 E)).arrowCongr
      (StrongDual.toWeakDual (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := StrongDual 𝕜 G))
      (m.arensFirst.flip q).toLinearMap
  cont := continuous_arensFirst_weakDual_left m q

/-- Changing views leaves the actual first Arens value unchanged. -/
@[simp] theorem arensFirstWeakLeft_apply (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G)
    (q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F)) (p : WeakDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E)) :
    m.arensFirstWeakLeft q p = StrongDual.toWeakDual (m.arensFirst p.toStrongDual q) := rfl

/-- The first weak-star map evaluates at the original iterated dual action. -/
@[simp] theorem arensFirstWeakLeft_apply_apply (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G)
    (q : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F)) (p : WeakDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E))
    (phi : StrongDual 𝕜 G) :
    m.arensFirstWeakLeft q p phi = p (m.dualBilinear.dualBilinear q phi) := rfl

/-- The actual second Arens extension in its continuous second weak-star variable. -/
def arensSecondWeakRight (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G)
    (p : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E)) :
    WeakDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F) →L[𝕜] WeakDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 G) where
  toLinearMap :=
    (StrongDual.toWeakDual (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := StrongDual 𝕜 F)).arrowCongr
      (StrongDual.toWeakDual (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := StrongDual 𝕜 G))
      (m.arensSecond p).toLinearMap
  cont := continuous_arensSecond_weakDual_right m p

/-- Changing views leaves the actual second Arens value unchanged. -/
@[simp] theorem arensSecondWeakRight_apply (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G)
    (p : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E)) (q : WeakDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F)) :
    m.arensSecondWeakRight p q = StrongDual.toWeakDual (m.arensSecond p q.toStrongDual) := rfl

/-- The second weak-star map retains the original second outer evaluation. -/
@[simp] theorem arensSecondWeakRight_apply_apply (m : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G)
    (p : StrongDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 E)) (q : WeakDual 𝕜 (StrongDual 𝕜 F))
    (phi : StrongDual 𝕜 G) :
    m.arensSecondWeakRight p q phi = q (m.flip.dualBilinear.dualBilinear p phi) := rfl

end ContinuousLinearMap

namespace WeakDual

variable {𝕜 : Type u} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [StarRing 𝕜] [NormedStarGroup 𝕜]
variable {A : Type v} [SeminormedAddCommGroup A] [StarAddMonoid A]
variable [NormedSpace 𝕜 A] [StarModule 𝕜 A] [NormedStarGroup A]

/-- The original conjugate-linear dual involution as a weak-star continuous equivalence. -/
def intrinsicStarContinuousLinearEquiv : WeakDual 𝕜 A ≃L⋆[𝕜] WeakDual 𝕜 A where
  toLinearEquiv :=
    ((toStrongDual (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := A)).trans
      (StrongDual.intrinsicStarIsometry (𝕜 := 𝕜) (A := A)).toLinearEquiv).trans
      (StrongDual.toWeakDual (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := A))
  continuous_toFun := by
    apply WeakDual.continuous_of_continuous_eval
    intro a
    change Continuous (fun phi : WeakDual 𝕜 A => star (phi (star a)))
    exact (WeakDual.eval_continuous (star a)).star
  continuous_invFun := by
    apply WeakDual.continuous_of_continuous_eval
    intro a
    change Continuous (fun phi : WeakDual 𝕜 A => star (phi (star a)))
    exact (WeakDual.eval_continuous (star a)).star

/-- Weak-star evaluation uses the original coefficient involution and scalar conjugation. -/
@[simp] theorem intrinsicStarContinuousLinearEquiv_apply (phi : WeakDual 𝕜 A) (a : A) :
    intrinsicStarContinuousLinearEquiv phi a = star (phi (star a)) := rfl

/-- The original normed view retains exactly the pre-existing dual involution. -/
@[simp] theorem intrinsicStarContinuousLinearEquiv_toStrongDual (phi : WeakDual 𝕜 A) :
    (intrinsicStarContinuousLinearEquiv phi).toStrongDual =
      StrongDual.intrinsicStarIsometry phi.toStrongDual := rfl

/-- The same original continuous-dual norm is preserved after changing views. -/
theorem intrinsicStarContinuousLinearEquiv_norm (phi : WeakDual 𝕜 A) :
    ‖(intrinsicStarContinuousLinearEquiv phi).toStrongDual‖ = ‖phi.toStrongDual‖ :=
  (StrongDual.intrinsicStarIsometry (𝕜 := 𝕜) (A := A)).norm_map phi.toStrongDual

end WeakDual

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Group.Uniform
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Seminorm.Norm
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Compact.Basic
public import Mathlib.Topology.Order.IsLUB

/-!
# Injective operators with a compact left-parametrix error

An injective continuous linear map with a continuous left regularizer modulo
actual compact operators is a closed topological embedding. The scalar field
and both normed spaces may be incomplete, and zero spaces are allowed.

The lower-bound argument uses the bounded-shell pattern from Mathlib's compact
Fredholm alternative, but uses injectivity of the original map, not a
non-eigenvalue or injectivity assumption on the composite. Both compactness
arguments produce limits in the original domain rather than in a completion.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Function Set Topology

universe u𝕜 uE uF

namespace ContinuousLinearMap

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
variable {E : Type uE} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
variable {F : Type uF} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]

/-- An injective map with compact left-parametrix error has a positive norm
lower bound, without a completeness or nontrivial-space assumption. -/
private theorem exists_pos_mul_norm_le_of_injective_compact_left_parametrix
    (S : E →L[𝕜] F) (V : F →L[𝕜] E) (hS : Function.Injective S)
    (hCompact : IsCompactOperator (V.comp S - (1 : E →L[𝕜] E))) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ z : E, c * ‖z‖ ≤ ‖S z‖ := by
  classical
  by_contra hNot
  have hFail (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ z : E, ‖S z‖ < ε * ‖z‖ := by
    by_contra hNo
    have hBound (z : E) : ε * ‖z‖ ≤ ‖S z‖ :=
      le_of_not_gt fun hz => hNo ⟨z, hz⟩
    exact hNot ⟨ε, hε, hBound⟩
  obtain ⟨ν, hν⟩ := NormedField.exists_one_lt_norm 𝕜
  let a : ℝ := ‖ν‖⁻¹
  have ha : 0 < a := inv_pos.mpr (zero_lt_one.trans hν)
  have hSmall (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
      ∃ z : E, ‖z‖ ≤ 1 ∧ a ≤ ‖z‖ ∧ ‖S z‖ < ε := by
    obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hFail ε hε
    have hzNe : z ≠ 0 := by
      intro hzZero
      subst z
      have hFalse : (0 : ℝ) < 0 := by
        simpa only [map_zero, norm_zero, mul_zero] using hz
      exact (lt_irrefl (0 : ℝ)) hFalse
    obtain ⟨d, hd, hUpper, hLower, _hInv⟩ :=
      rescale_to_shell (c := ν) (ε := (1 : ℝ)) (x := z)
        hν zero_lt_one hzNe
    refine ⟨d • z, hUpper.le, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simpa only [a, one_div] using hLower
    · calc
        ‖S (d • z)‖ = ‖d‖ * ‖S z‖ := by rw [map_smul, norm_smul]
        _ < ‖d‖ * (ε * ‖z‖) :=
          mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hz (norm_pos_iff.mpr hd)
        _ = ε * ‖d • z‖ := by
          rw [norm_smul]
          exact mul_left_comm _ _ _
        _ ≤ ε := by
          simpa only [mul_one] using
            mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hUpper.le hε.le
  obtain ⟨δ, _hδanti, hδpos, hδlim⟩ := exists_seq_strictAnti_tendsto (0 : ℝ)
  let x : ℕ → E := fun n => Classical.choose (hSmall (δ n) (hδpos n))
  have hx (n : ℕ) : ‖x n‖ ≤ 1 ∧ a ≤ ‖x n‖ ∧ ‖S (x n)‖ < δ n :=
    Classical.choose_spec (hSmall (δ n) (hδpos n))
  have hS0 : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => S (x n)) atTop (𝓝 (0 : F)) :=
    squeeze_zero_norm (fun n => (hx n).2.2.le) hδlim
  let C : E →L[𝕜] E := V.comp S - 1
  have hC : IsCompactOperator C := hCompact
  obtain ⟨K, hK, hKimage⟩ :=
    IsCompactOperator.image_closedBall_subset_compact
      (f := C.toLinearMap) hC (1 : ℝ)
  have hKmem (n : ℕ) : C (x n) ∈ K :=
    hKimage ⟨x n, mem_closedBall_zero_iff.mpr (hx n).1, rfl⟩
  obtain ⟨k, _hkK, ψ, hψ, hCxψ⟩ :=
    hK.tendsto_subseq (x := fun n : ℕ => C (x n)) hKmem
  have hIdentity (z : E) : V (S z) - C z = z := by
    change V (S z) - (V (S z) - z) = z
    exact sub_sub_cancel _ _
  have hVSψ0 : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => V (S (x (ψ n)))) atTop (𝓝 (0 : E)) := by
    simpa only [map_zero, Function.comp_def] using
      (V.continuous.tendsto (0 : F)).comp (hS0.comp hψ.tendsto_atTop)
  have hXlim : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => x (ψ n)) atTop (𝓝 (-k)) := by
    simpa only [Function.comp_def, hIdentity, zero_sub] using hVSψ0.sub hCxψ
  have hSk : S (-k) = 0 :=
    tendsto_nhds_unique
      ((S.continuous.tendsto (-k)).comp hXlim)
      (hS0.comp hψ.tendsto_atTop)
  have hNeg : -k = (0 : E) := hS (by simpa only [map_zero] using hSk)
  have hkZero : k = 0 := neg_eq_zero.mp hNeg
  have hX0 : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => x (ψ n)) atTop (𝓝 (0 : E)) := by
    simpa only [hkZero, neg_zero] using hXlim
  rw [NormedAddGroup.tendsto_nhds_zero] at hX0
  have hBad : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, False :=
    (hX0 a ha).mono fun n hn => (not_lt_of_ge (hx (ψ n)).2.1) hn
  simp only [Filter.eventually_const] at hBad

/-- An injective continuous linear map with an actual compact left-parametrix
error is a closed topological embedding. Neither ambient space nor the scalar
field need be complete, and the left regularizer need not be injective. -/
theorem isClosedEmbedding_of_injective_compact_left_parametrix
    (S : E →L[𝕜] F) (V : F →L[𝕜] E) (hS : Function.Injective S)
    (hCompact : IsCompactOperator (V.comp S - (1 : E →L[𝕜] E))) :
    Topology.IsClosedEmbedding S := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨c, hc, hBound⟩ :=
    exists_pos_mul_norm_le_of_injective_compact_left_parametrix S V hS hCompact
  obtain ⟨A, hA⟩ : ∃ A : NNReal, AntilipschitzWith A S :=
    antilipschitzWith_iff_exists_mul_le_norm.mpr ⟨c, hc, hBound⟩
  have hEmbed : Topology.IsEmbedding S := hA.isEmbedding S.continuous
  refine { hEmbed with isClosed_range := ?_ }
  apply isClosed_of_closure_subset
  intro y hy
  obtain ⟨z, hzRange, hzlim⟩ := mem_closure_iff_seq_limit.mp hy
  let x : ℕ → E := fun n => Classical.choose (hzRange n)
  have hx (n : ℕ) : S (x n) = z n := Classical.choose_spec (hzRange n)
  have hSx : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => S (x n)) atTop (𝓝 y) := by
    simpa only [hx] using hzlim
  have hSbound : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ‖S (x n)‖ ≤ ‖y‖ + 1 :=
    hSx.norm.eventually_le_const (lt_add_of_pos_right _ zero_lt_one)
  let r : ℝ := (‖y‖ + 1) / c
  have hxBall : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, x n ∈ Metric.closedBall (0 : E) r := by
    refine hSbound.mono ?_
    intro n hn
    apply mem_closedBall_zero_iff.mpr
    dsimp only [r]
    apply (le_div_iff₀ hc).mpr
    simpa only [mul_comm] using (hBound (x n)).trans hn
  let C : E →L[𝕜] E := V.comp S - 1
  have hC : IsCompactOperator C := hCompact
  obtain ⟨K, hK, hKimage⟩ :=
    IsCompactOperator.image_closedBall_subset_compact (f := C.toLinearMap) hC r
  have hCK : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, C (x n) ∈ K :=
    hxBall.mono fun n hn => hKimage ⟨x n, hn, rfl⟩
  obtain ⟨k, _hkK, ψ, hψ, hCxψ⟩ := hK.tendsto_subseq' hCK.frequently
  have hIdentity (t : E) : V (S t) - C t = t := by
    change V (S t) - (V (S t) - t) = t
    exact sub_sub_cancel _ _
  have hXlim : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => x (ψ n)) atTop (𝓝 (V y - k)) := by
    simpa only [Function.comp_def, hIdentity] using
      ((V.continuous.tendsto y).comp (hSx.comp hψ.tendsto_atTop)).sub hCxψ
  have hPreimage : S (V y - k) = y :=
    tendsto_nhds_unique
      ((S.continuous.tendsto (V y - k)).comp hXlim)
      (hSx.comp hψ.tendsto_atTop)
  exact ⟨V y - k, hPreimage⟩

end ContinuousLinearMap

Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import MathlibExt.Topology.Algebra.Module.Matrix
public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Compact.Pi

/-!
# Compactness of rectangular operator matrices

A compact map on the existing product-topological PiLp carrier has compact
recovered coefficients, even for arbitrary index types. For finite rows and
columns, compactness of the column action is equivalent to compactness of all
entries. Reconstruction retains continuity of addition in the target, needed
for the finite sums of compact entry maps.

The statements use semiring scalars and topological additive groups with
modules. No norm, completeness, separation or scalar-continuity hypothesis
is required, and no infinite square-summable-space topology is asserted.
-/

public section

open scoped BigOperators

universe uR uM uN uE uF

variable {R : Type uR} [Semiring R]
variable {m : Type uM} {n : Type uN}
variable {E : Type uE} {F : Type uF}
variable [AddCommGroup E] [TopologicalSpace E] [Module R E]
variable [AddCommGroup F] [TopologicalSpace F] [Module R F]

/-- Each recovered coefficient of a compact PiLp operator is compact.
Neither index type needs to be finite, and target addition need not be continuous. -/
theorem IsCompactOperator.toPiLpMatrix [DecidableEq n]
    {T : PiLp 2 (fun _ : n => E) →L[R] PiLp 2 (fun _ : m => F)}
    (hT : IsCompactOperator T) (i : m) (j : n) :
    IsCompactOperator (T.toPiLpMatrix i j) := by
  let J : E →L[R] PiLp 2 (fun _ : n => E) :=
    (PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 R (fun _ : n => E)).symm.toContinuousLinearMap.comp
      (ContinuousLinearMap.single R (fun _ : n => E) j)
  let P : PiLp 2 (fun _ : m => F) →L[R] F :=
    (ContinuousLinearMap.proj i : (m → F) →L[R] F).comp
      (PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 R (fun _ : m => F)).toContinuousLinearMap
  have hEntry : T.toPiLpMatrix i j = P.comp (T.comp J) := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro x
    rw [ContinuousLinearMap.toPiLpMatrix_apply]
    rfl
  rw [hEntry]
  exact (hT.comp_clm J).clm_comp P

/-- The finite-row column action is compact exactly when all its entries are compact. -/
theorem Matrix.isCompactOperator_toPiLpContinuousLinearMap_iff [Finite m] [Fintype n]
    [ContinuousAdd F] (M : Matrix m n (E →L[R] F)) :
    IsCompactOperator M.toPiLpContinuousLinearMap ↔
      ∀ (i : m) (j : n), IsCompactOperator (M i j) := by
  classical
  constructor
  · intro hM i j
    simpa only [ContinuousLinearMap.toPiLpMatrix_toPiLpContinuousLinearMap] using
      (hM.toPiLpMatrix i j)
  · intro hEntries
    let P (j : n) : PiLp 2 (fun _ : n => E) →L[R] E :=
      (ContinuousLinearMap.proj j : (n → E) →L[R] E).comp
        (PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 R (fun _ : n => E)).toContinuousLinearMap
    have hRows (i : m) : IsCompactOperator
        (fun v : PiLp 2 (fun _ : n => E) => ∑ j : n, M i j (v j)) := by
      have hFactors (j : n) : IsCompactOperator
          (fun v : PiLp 2 (fun _ : n => E) => M i j (v j)) := by
        change IsCompactOperator ((M i j) ∘ P j)
        exact (hEntries i j).comp_clm (P j)
      have hSum : IsCompactOperator
          (∑ j : n, (fun v : PiLp 2 (fun _ : n => E) => M i j (v j))) := by
        refine Finset.sum_induction (s := Finset.univ)
          (fun j : n => fun v : PiLp 2 (fun _ : n => E) => M i j (v j))
          (fun f : PiLp 2 (fun _ : n => E) → F => IsCompactOperator f)
          ?_ ?_ (fun j _ => hFactors j)
        · intro f g hf hg
          exact hf.add hg
        · exact isCompactOperator_zero
      simpa only [Finset.sum_fn] using hSum
    have hProduct : IsCompactOperator
        (fun v : PiLp 2 (fun _ : n => E) => WithLp.ofLp (M.toPiLpContinuousLinearMap v)) := by
      apply (isCompactOperator_pi_iff _).mpr
      intro i
      change IsCompactOperator
        (fun v : PiLp 2 (fun _ : n => E) => M.toPiLpContinuousLinearMap v i)
      simpa only [Matrix.toPiLpContinuousLinearMap_apply] using hRows i
    simpa only [Function.comp_def, WithLp.toLp_ofLp] using
      (hProduct.continuous_comp (PiLp.continuous_toLp 2 (fun _ : m => F)))

/-- A PiLp operator with finite source and target indices is compact exactly
when every recovered coefficient is compact. -/
theorem ContinuousLinearMap.isCompactOperator_iff_toPiLpMatrix
    [Finite m] [Finite n] [DecidableEq n] [ContinuousAdd F]
    (T : PiLp 2 (fun _ : n => E) →L[R] PiLp 2 (fun _ : m => F)) :
    IsCompactOperator T ↔ ∀ (i : m) (j : n), IsCompactOperator (T.toPiLpMatrix i j) := by
  constructor
  · intro hT i j
    exact hT.toPiLpMatrix i j
  · intro hEntries
    let : Fintype n := Fintype.ofFinite n
    have hAction : IsCompactOperator T.toPiLpMatrix.toPiLpContinuousLinearMap :=
      (Matrix.isCompactOperator_toPiLpContinuousLinearMap_iff T.toPiLpMatrix).mpr hEntries
    simpa only [Matrix.toPiLpContinuousLinearMap_toPiLpMatrix] using hAction

/-
Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Compact.FiniteDimension

/-!
# Compact open operators have finite-dimensional targets

An open compact continuous linear map has finite-dimensional target over a
complete nontrivially normed scalar field. Neither ambient space is assumed
complete, and surjectivity is unnecessary. The proof uses the stock Riesz
criterion on an actual compact neighborhood of zero in the target.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Set Topology

universe u𝕜 uE uF

namespace FiniteDimensional

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [CompleteSpace 𝕜]
variable {E : Type uE} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
variable {F : Type uF} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]

/-- An open compact continuous linear map has finite-dimensional target.
Only the scalar field, not either ambient space, is assumed complete. -/
theorem of_isCompactOperator_of_isOpenMap (f : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (hCompact : IsCompactOperator f) (hOpen : IsOpenMap f) : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 F := by
  obtain ⟨K, hK, hPre⟩ := hCompact
  have hImage : f '' (f ⁻¹' K) ∈ 𝓝 (0 : F) := by
    simpa only [map_zero] using hOpen.image_mem_nhds hPre
  have hK0 : K ∈ 𝓝 (0 : F) :=
    mem_of_superset hImage (image_preimage_subset f K)
  exact FiniteDimensional.of_totallyBounded_nhds_zero 𝕜 hK0 hK.totallyBounded

end FiniteDimensional

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Compact.Basic
public import Mathlib.Topology.Compactness.Compact
public import Mathlib.Order.Filter.Finite

/-!
# Compact operators into dependent products

Coordinate extraction works for arbitrary products. For a finite product,
coordinate compactness is also sufficient: finitely many source neighborhoods
can be synchronized and the product of the coordinate witnesses is compact.

These statements use the stock predicate on arbitrary functions, with only
a zero and topology on the source and topologies on the components. They do
not require target algebra, continuity of the function or preservation of zero.
-/

public section

open Set Filter
open scoped Topology

universe uX uI uB

variable {X : Type uX} [Zero X] [TopologicalSpace X]
variable {ι : Type uI} {β : ι → Type uB} [∀ i, TopologicalSpace (β i)]

/-- Each coordinate of a compact operator into a dependent product is compact.
The index type need not be finite. -/
theorem IsCompactOperator.eval {f : X → ∀ i, β i}
    (hf : IsCompactOperator f) (i : ι) :
    IsCompactOperator (fun x => f x i) := by
  rcases hf with ⟨K, hK, hPreimage⟩
  refine ⟨Function.eval i '' K, hK.image (continuous_apply i), ?_⟩
  exact Filter.mem_of_superset hPreimage fun x hx => ⟨f x, hx, rfl⟩

/-- An arbitrary function into a finite dependent product is a compact operator
if and only if each coordinate is a compact operator. -/
theorem isCompactOperator_pi_iff [Finite ι] (f : X → ∀ i, β i) :
    IsCompactOperator f ↔ ∀ i, IsCompactOperator (fun x => f x i) := by
  constructor
  · intro hf i
    exact hf.eval i
  · intro hCoordinates
    have hWitnesses : ∀ i, ∃ K : Set (β i), IsCompact K ∧
        (fun x => f x i) ⁻¹' K ∈ (𝓝 0 : Filter X) := hCoordinates
    let K (i : ι) : Set (β i) := Classical.choose (hWitnesses i)
    have hK : ∀ i, IsCompact (K i) :=
      fun i => (Classical.choose_spec (hWitnesses i)).1
    have hNeighborhoods : ∀ i, (fun x => f x i) ⁻¹' K i ∈ (𝓝 0 : Filter X) :=
      fun i => (Classical.choose_spec (hWitnesses i)).2
    refine ⟨{y : ∀ i, β i | ∀ i, y i ∈ K i}, isCompact_pi_infinite hK, ?_⟩
    have hPreimage : f ⁻¹' {y : ∀ i, β i | ∀ i, y i ∈ K i} =
        ⋂ i, (fun x => f x i) ⁻¹' K i := by
      ext x
      simp only [Set.mem_preimage, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, Set.mem_iInter]
    rw [hPreimage]
    exact Filter.iInter_mem.mpr hNeighborhoods

Author: @toskua

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Completion
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Extend

/-!
# Actual completion of a linear isometry equivalence

Complete the original forward and inverse stock isometries. Dense original
coefficients and continuity prove their inverse laws on the full completions.
The actual maps and norms are retained, with independent universes and zero
spaces allowed. This supplies completion of the actual tensor congruence and
associator used by the original mixed-factor Radon product constructor.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open UniformSpace

namespace LinearIsometryEquiv

noncomputable section

universe u𝕜 uE uF

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [NormedField 𝕜]
variable {E : Type uE} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
variable {F : Type uF} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]

/-- Complete an actual linear isometry equivalence using its stock forward and inverse completion maps. -/
def completion (e : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] F) : Completion E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] Completion F := by
  let _ : UniformContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 E :=
    uniformContinuousConstSMul_of_continuousConstSMul 𝕜 E
  let _ : UniformContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 F :=
    uniformContinuousConstSMul_of_continuousConstSMul 𝕜 F
  let f := e.toLinearIsometry.completion
  let g := e.symm.toLinearIsometry.completion
  have hfg : f.toLinearMap.comp g.toLinearMap = LinearMap.id := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro z
    change f (g z) = z
    refine Completion.induction_on z
      (isClosed_eq (f.continuous.comp g.continuous) continuous_id) ?_
    intro z
    change e.toLinearIsometry.completion
        (e.symm.toLinearIsometry.completion (z : Completion F)) = (z : Completion F)
    rw [LinearIsometry.completion_apply_coe, LinearIsometry.completion_apply_coe]
    exact congrArg (fun z : F => (z : Completion F)) (e.apply_symm_apply z)
  have hgf : g.toLinearMap.comp f.toLinearMap = LinearMap.id := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro z
    change g (f z) = z
    refine Completion.induction_on z
      (isClosed_eq (g.continuous.comp f.continuous) continuous_id) ?_
    intro z
    change e.symm.toLinearIsometry.completion
        (e.toLinearIsometry.completion (z : Completion E)) = (z : Completion E)
    rw [LinearIsometry.completion_apply_coe, LinearIsometry.completion_apply_coe]
    exact congrArg (fun z : E => (z : Completion E)) (e.symm_apply_apply z)
  exact LinearIsometryEquiv.ofLinearIsometry f g.toLinearMap hfg hgf

/-- The actual completed equivalence retains the literal original coefficient value. -/
theorem completion_apply_coe (e : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] F) (z : E) :
    completion e (z : Completion E) = (e z : Completion F) := by
  let _ : UniformContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 E :=
    uniformContinuousConstSMul_of_continuousConstSMul 𝕜 E
  let _ : UniformContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 F :=
    uniformContinuousConstSMul_of_continuousConstSMul 𝕜 F
  change e.toLinearIsometry.completion (z : Completion E) = (e z : Completion F)
  exact LinearIsometry.completion_apply_coe _ _

/-- The inverse completed equivalence retains the literal original inverse coefficient value. -/
theorem completion_symm_apply_coe (e : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] F) (z : F) :
    (completion e).symm (z : Completion F) = (e.symm z : Completion E) := by
  let _ : UniformContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 E :=
    uniformContinuousConstSMul_of_continuousConstSMul 𝕜 E
  let _ : UniformContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 F :=
    uniformContinuousConstSMul_of_continuousConstSMul 𝕜 F
  change e.symm.toLinearIsometry.completion (z : Completion F) = (e.symm z : Completion E)
  exact LinearIsometry.completion_apply_coe _ _


/-- The actual completed equivalence has the stock forward completion linear-map DATA. -/
theorem completion_toLinearMap (e : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] F) :
    letI : UniformContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 E :=
      uniformContinuousConstSMul_of_continuousConstSMul 𝕜 E
    letI : UniformContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 F :=
      uniformContinuousConstSMul_of_continuousConstSMul 𝕜 F
    (e.completion).toLinearMap = e.toLinearIsometry.completion.toLinearMap := rfl

/-- The actual inverse completed equivalence has the stock inverse completion linear-map DATA. -/
theorem completion_symm_toLinearMap (e : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] F) :
    letI : UniformContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 E :=
      uniformContinuousConstSMul_of_continuousConstSMul 𝕜 E
    letI : UniformContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 F :=
      uniformContinuousConstSMul_of_continuousConstSMul 𝕜 F
    (e.completion).symm.toLinearMap = e.symm.toLinearIsometry.completion.toLinearMap := rfl

end

end LinearIsometryEquiv

Author: @toskua

module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Operator.DualLowerBound

/-!
# Actual controlled approximate preimages from the literal dual norm lower bound

The derived half-ball closure gives an actual unit-ball preimage whose
image approximates a normalized original target vector. Positive real
scaling gives approximation error≤‖y‖/2 and preimage norm≤2‖y‖. The zero
target case is handled by the original zero map law. No preimage, quotient,
surjectivity, closed range or model certificate is input.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open Metric Set

namespace ContinuousLinearMap

noncomputable section

universe u v

variable {E : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E]
variable {F : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F]

/-- Original dual norm lower bound gives genuine controlled approximate preimages for every target vector. -/
theorem exists_controlled_approx_preimage_of_dual_lower_bound (B : E →L[ℂ] F)
    (hdual : ∀ G : StrongDual ℂ F, ‖G‖ ≤ ‖G.comp B‖) (y : F) :
    ∃ x : E, dist (B x) y ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) * ‖y‖ ∧ ‖x‖ ≤ 2 * ‖y‖ := by
  by_cases hy : y = 0
  · refine ⟨0, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> simp only [hy, map_zero, dist_self, norm_zero, mul_zero, le_refl]
  · let : NormedSpace ℝ E := NormedSpace.restrictScalars ℝ ℂ E
    let : NormedSpace ℝ F := NormedSpace.restrictScalars ℝ ℂ F
    let t : ℝ := 2 * ‖y‖
    have ht : 0 < t := mul_pos (by norm_num) (norm_pos_iff.mpr hy)
    let z : F := t⁻¹ • y
    have hz : ‖z‖ ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) := by
      change ‖t⁻¹ • y‖ ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ)
      rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (inv_pos.mpr ht)]
      dsimp only [t]
      field_simp
      ring_nf
      exact le_rfl
    have hclosure := B.halfBall_subset_closure_image_unitBall_of_dual_lower_bound hdual
      (mem_closedBall_zero_iff.mpr hz)
    obtain ⟨v, ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩, hv⟩ := Metric.mem_closure_iff.mp hclosure (1 / 4) (by norm_num)
    have hyz : t • z = y := by
      change t • (t⁻¹ • y) = y
      rw [smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ ht.ne', one_smul]
    refine ⟨t • w, ?_, ?_⟩
    · have hdist : dist (B (t • w)) y = t * dist (B w) z := by
        rw [B.map_smul_of_tower, ← hyz, dist_eq_norm, ← smul_sub,
          norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos ht, dist_eq_norm]
      rw [hdist]
      have hsmall : dist (B w) z < (1 / 4 : ℝ) := by
        simpa only [dist_comm] using hv
      have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hsmall.le ht.le
      dsimp only [t] at h ⊢
      nlinarith
    · rw [norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos ht]
      have hwNorm : ‖w‖ ≤ 1 := mem_closedBall_zero_iff.mp hw
      exact (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hwNorm ht.le).trans_eq (mul_one t)

end

end ContinuousLinearMap

Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.LocallyConvex.Separation
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Banach
public import Mathlib.Basic.Complex.Basic
public import Mathlib.Analysis.RCLike.Basic
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Basic

/-!
# A literal dual-precomposition lower bound gives an actual approximate unit-ball image

For an original complex bounded linear map B, the inequality
‖F‖≤‖F∘B‖ for every actual continuous linear functional F implies that
the image of the original closed unit ball is norm dense in a fixed
positive-radius target ball. Separation from that convex closed image
would give a functional contradicting the original dual norm inequality.
No predual quotient, surjectivity, range-closure or model certificate is
an input. This is the approximation prerequisite for the quotient constructor.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open Metric Set

namespace ContinuousLinearMap

noncomputable section

universe u v

variable {E : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E]
variable {F : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F]

/-- An actual dual norm lower bound gives the original target half-ball in the closed unit-ball image. -/
theorem halfBall_subset_closure_image_unitBall_of_dual_lower_bound (B : E →L[ℂ] F)
    (hdual : ∀ G : StrongDual ℂ F, ‖G‖ ≤ ‖G.comp B‖) :
    closedBall (0 : F) (1 / 2 : ℝ) ⊆ closure (B '' closedBall (0 : E) 1) := by
  let : NormedSpace ℝ E := NormedSpace.restrictScalars ℝ ℂ E
  let : NormedSpace ℝ F := NormedSpace.restrictScalars ℝ ℂ F
  intro y hy
  by_contra hnot
  let C : Set F := closure (B '' closedBall (0 : E) 1)
  have hconvex : Convex ℝ C :=
    ((convex_closedBall (0 : E) 1).linear_image (B.toLinearMap.restrictScalars ℝ)).closure
  have hzero : (0 : F) ∈ C := subset_closure ⟨0, by simp, B.map_zero⟩
  obtain ⟨G, r, hC, hGy⟩ := RCLike.geometric_hahn_banach_closed_point
    (𝕜 := ℂ) hconvex isClosed_closure hnot
  have hr : 0 < r := by
    have h := hC 0 hzero
    simpa only [map_zero, Complex.zero_re] using h
  let L : StrongDual ℂ E := G.comp B
  have hunit (x : E) (hx : ‖x‖ = 1) : ‖L x‖ ≤ r := by
    obtain ⟨c, hc, hphase⟩ := RCLike.exists_norm_eq_mul_self (L x)
    have hmem : c • x ∈ closedBall (0 : E) 1 := by
      rw [mem_closedBall_zero_iff, norm_smul, hc, hx, one_mul]
    have hvalue := hC (B (c • x)) (subset_closure ⟨c • x, hmem, rfl⟩)
    have hreal : (G (B (c • x))).re = ‖L x‖ := by
      change (L (c • x)).re = ‖L x‖
      rw [L.map_smul, smul_eq_mul, ← hphase]
      exact Complex.ofReal_re _
    change (G (B (c • x))).re < r at hvalue
    rw [hreal] at hvalue
    exact hvalue.le
  have hL : ‖L‖ ≤ r := L.opNorm_le_of_unit_norm hr.le hunit
  have hG : ‖G‖ ≤ r := (hdual G).trans hL
  have hynorm : ‖y‖ ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) := mem_closedBall_zero_iff.mp hy
  have hpoint : (G y).re ≤ ‖G‖ * (1 / 2 : ℝ) :=
    (Complex.re_le_norm _).trans ((G.le_opNorm y).trans
      (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hynorm (norm_nonneg G)))
  change r < (G y).re at hGy
  nlinarith [norm_nonneg G]

end

end ContinuousLinearMap

/-
Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Operator.DualApproximatePreimage

/-!
# Actual exact Banach preimages from the original dual norm lower bound

The proved controlled approximation is iterated on the original residual.
Its errors decrease geometrically, while its actual preimages form a
summable series in the original complete source. The series sum maps to
the original target and has the proved norm bound. No exact preimage,
surjectivity, quotient, closed range or model certificate is an input.
This constructs the preimage prerequisite for the actual predual quotient.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open Filter Set
open scoped Topology BigOperators

namespace ContinuousLinearMap

noncomputable section

universe u v

variable {E : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] [CompleteSpace E]
variable {F : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F]

/-- An original dual norm lower bound constructs exact preimages with a proved Banach norm bound. -/
theorem exists_preimage_norm_le_of_dual_lower_bound (B : E →L[ℂ] F)
    (hdual : ∀ G : StrongDual ℂ F, ‖G‖ ≤ ‖G.comp B‖) (y : F) :
    ∃ x : E, B x = y ∧ ‖x‖ ≤ 5 * ‖y‖ := by
  classical
  choose g hg using fun z : F => B.exists_controlled_approx_preimage_of_dual_lower_bound hdual z
  let h (z : F) := z - B (g z)
  have hle (z : F) : ‖h z‖ ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) * ‖z‖ := by
    rw [← dist_eq_norm, dist_comm]
    exact (hg z).1
  have hnle (n : ℕ) : ‖h^[n] y‖ ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ n * ‖y‖ := by
    induction n with
    | zero => simp only [Function.iterate_zero_apply, pow_zero, one_mul, le_refl]
    | succ n ih =>
      rw [Function.iterate_succ']
      apply (hle _).trans
      rw [pow_succ', mul_assoc]
      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ih (by norm_num)
  let u (n : ℕ) : E := g (h^[n] y)
  have ule (n : ℕ) : ‖u n‖ ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ n * (2 * ‖y‖) := by
    calc
      ‖u n‖ ≤ 2 * ‖h^[n] y‖ := (hg _).2
      _ ≤ 2 * ((1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ n * ‖y‖) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hnle n) (by norm_num)
      _ = (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ n * (2 * ‖y‖) := by ring
  have sn : Summable (fun n => ‖u n‖) :=
    Summable.of_nonneg_of_le (fun n => norm_nonneg (u n)) ule
      (Summable.mul_right _ summable_geometric_two)
  have su : Summable u := sn.of_norm
  let x : E := ∑' n, u n
  have hnorm : ‖x‖ ≤ 5 * ‖y‖ := by
    calc
      ‖x‖ ≤ ∑' n, ‖u n‖ := norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm sn
      _ ≤ ∑' n, (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ n * (2 * ‖y‖) :=
        sn.tsum_le_tsum ule (Summable.mul_right _ summable_geometric_two)
      _ = (∑' n, (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ n) * (2 * ‖y‖) := tsum_mul_right
      _ = 4 * ‖y‖ := by rw [tsum_geometric_two]; ring
      _ ≤ 5 * ‖y‖ := by nlinarith [norm_nonneg y]
  have hsum (n : ℕ) : B (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, u i) = y - h^[n] y := by
    induction n with
    | zero => simp only [Finset.range_zero, Finset.sum_empty, map_zero, Function.iterate_zero_apply, sub_self]
    | succ n ih =>
      rw [Finset.sum_range_succ, B.map_add, ih, Function.iterate_succ_apply', sub_add]
  have hsumLimit : Tendsto (fun n => ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, u i) atTop (𝓝 x) :=
    su.hasSum.tendsto_sum_nat
  have himageLimit : Tendsto (fun n => B (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, u i)) atTop (𝓝 (B x)) :=
    (B.continuous.tendsto x).comp hsumLimit
  have hresidual : Tendsto (fun n => h^[n] y) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
    rw [tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero]
    simp only [sub_zero]
    apply squeeze_zero (fun n => norm_nonneg (h^[n] y)) hnle
    have hpow := (_root_.tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one
      (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 2) (by norm_num : (1 / 2 : ℝ) < 1)).mul
      (tendsto_const_nhds : Tendsto (fun _n : ℕ => ‖y‖) atTop _)
    simpa only [zero_mul] using hpow
  have htarget : Tendsto (fun n => y - h^[n] y) atTop (𝓝 y) := by
    simpa only [sub_zero] using
      (tendsto_const_nhds : Tendsto (fun _n : ℕ => y) atTop _).sub hresidual
  rw [show (fun n => B (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, u i)) = (fun n => y - h^[n] y) from funext hsum]
    at himageLimit
  exact ⟨x, tendsto_nhds_unique himageLimit htarget, hnorm⟩

/-- The same original bounded map is surjective, with no quotient or closed-range premise. -/
theorem surjective_of_dual_lower_bound (B : E →L[ℂ] F)
    (hdual : ∀ G : StrongDual ℂ F, ‖G‖ ≤ ‖G.comp B‖) : Function.Surjective B := by
  intro y
  obtain ⟨x, hxy, _hnorm⟩ := B.exists_preimage_norm_le_of_dual_lower_bound hdual y
  exact ⟨x, hxy⟩

end

end ContinuousLinearMap

Author: @toskua, Avocado
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.LinearMap.FiniteRange
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Basic
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.SimpleModule.Basic

/-!
# Bounded finite-rank operators

The scalar-general carrier reuses Mathlib's finite-range submodule by comapping
along the continuous-linear-map inclusion. The original normed domain and
range and nontrivially normed field are unchanged. Over a field, noetherian
range and finitely generated range are equivalent; the membership theorem
retains the source finite-range characterization.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

namespace ContinuousLinearMap

universe u𝕜 uE uF
variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
variable {E : Type uE} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
variable {F : Type uF} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]

/-- Bounded finite-rank operators are the comap of Mathlib's finite-range submodule. -/
abbrev finiteRankOperator : Submodule 𝕜 (E →L[𝕜] F) :=
  (LinearMap.finiteRange 𝕜 E F).comap (ContinuousLinearMap.coeLM 𝕜)

/-- Membership is the finite-range property on the same underlying linear map.
Use this equivalence explicitly: stock comap simp rules already normalize its left side. -/
theorem mem_finiteRankOperator (T : E →L[𝕜] F) :
    T ∈ finiteRankOperator (𝕜 := 𝕜) ↔ T.toLinearMap.HasFiniteRange := by
  change T.toLinearMap.HasNoetherianRange ↔ T.toLinearMap.HasFiniteRange
  exact ⟨fun h => h.hasFiniteRange, fun h => h.hasNoetherianRange⟩

/-- Compatibility with the canonical noetherian-range comap over the same field. -/
theorem finiteRankOperator_eq_comap_finiteRange :
    finiteRankOperator (𝕜 := 𝕜) (E := E) (F := F) =
      (LinearMap.finiteRange 𝕜 E F).comap (ContinuousLinearMap.coeLM 𝕜) :=
  rfl

end ContinuousLinearMap

/-
Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Compact.LeftRegularizer
public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Compact.OpenMap
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Fredholm.Basic
public import Mathlib.Analysis.LocallyConvex.HahnBanach
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Group.Quotient

import Mathlib.Tactic.Abel

/-!
# Compact parametrices on normed spaces

An actual two-sided compact parametrix implies all five strong Fredholm
properties on independently typed real-like or complex-like normed spaces.
Neither ambient space needs completeness or an inner product. The scalar
dictionary is derived from the original normed field without changing its norm.

The kernel is finite-dimensional and continuously complemented. The actual
restriction to a complement is closed embedded, and projection factorization
transfers strictness and closed range. The actual range quotient is compact
and open, hence finite-dimensional. No approximation property is assumed.
-/

namespace ContinuousLinearMap.IsFredholm

universe u𝕜 uE uF

section FiniteKernel

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [CompleteSpace 𝕜]
variable {E : Type uE} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
variable {F : Type uF} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]

private theorem finiteDimensional_ker_of_compact_left_error
    (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (U : F →L[𝕜] E)
    (hUT : IsCompactOperator (U.comp T - (1 : E →L[𝕜] E))) :
    FiniteDimensional 𝕜 T.ker := by
  let K : E →L[𝕜] E := U.comp T - 1
  have hK : IsCompactOperator K.toLinearMap := hUT
  have hPreserves : ∀ x ∈ T.ker, K.toLinearMap x ∈ T.ker := by
    intro x hx
    have hxT : T x = 0 := hx
    change T (U (T x) - x) = 0
    simp only [hxT, map_zero, map_sub, sub_self]
  have hRestricted : IsCompactOperator (K.toLinearMap.restrict hPreserves) :=
    hK.restrict hPreserves T.isClosed_ker
  have hNeg := hRestricted.neg
  change IsCompactOperator
    (fun x : T.ker => -(K.toLinearMap.restrict hPreserves x)) at hNeg
  have hIdentity :
      (fun x : T.ker => -(K.toLinearMap.restrict hPreserves x)) = id := by
    funext x
    apply Subtype.ext
    change -(U (T (x : E)) - (x : E)) = (x : E)
    rw [show T (x : E) = 0 from x.property, map_zero, zero_sub, neg_neg]
  have hId : IsCompactOperator (id : T.ker → T.ker) := hIdentity ▸ hNeg
  exact FiniteDimensional.of_isCompactOperator_id hId

end FiniteKernel

@[expose] public section

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [NormedField 𝕜] [IsRCLikeNormedField 𝕜]
variable {E : Type uE} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
variable {F : Type uF} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]

/-- A two-sided compact parametrix gives the actual strong Fredholm predicate.
The compatible scalar structure preserves the original normed field; no
completeness or inner product on either ambient space is required. -/
theorem of_compactParametrix (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (U : F →L[𝕜] E)
    (hUT : IsCompactOperator (U.comp T - (1 : E →L[𝕜] E)))
    (hTU : IsCompactOperator (T.comp U - (1 : F →L[𝕜] F))) :
    letI : RCLike 𝕜 := IsRCLikeNormedField.rclike 𝕜;
    T.IsFredholm := by
  let : RCLike 𝕜 := IsRCLikeNormedField.rclike 𝕜
  change T.IsFredholm
  have hFinite : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 T.ker :=
    finiteDimensional_ker_of_compact_left_error T U hUT
  let : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 T.ker := hFinite
  have hComplement : T.ker.ClosedComplemented :=
    Submodule.ClosedComplemented.of_finiteDimensional T.ker
  obtain ⟨H, hNH⟩ := hComplement.exists_isTopCompl
  let i : H →L[𝕜] E := H.subtypeL
  let r : E →L[𝕜] H := H.projectionOntoL T.ker hNH.symm
  let S : H →L[𝕜] F := T.domRestrict H
  let V : F →L[𝕜] H := r.comp U
  have hFix (x : H) : r (x : E) = x :=
    Submodule.projectionOntoL_apply_left hNH.symm x
  have hInjective : Function.Injective S := by
    intro x y hxy
    apply Subtype.ext
    have hTxy : T (x : E) = T (y : E) := hxy
    have hKer : (x : E) - (y : E) ∈ T.ker := by
      change T ((x : E) - (y : E)) = 0
      rw [map_sub, hTxy, sub_self]
    have hH : (x : E) - (y : E) ∈ H := H.sub_mem x.property y.property
    exact sub_eq_zero.mp
      ((Submodule.disjoint_def.mp hNH.isCompl.disjoint) _ hKer hH)
  have hError : V.comp S - (1 : H →L[𝕜] H) =
      r.comp ((U.comp T - (1 : E →L[𝕜] E)).comp i) := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro x
    change r (U (T (x : E))) - x = r (U (T (x : E)) - (x : E))
    rw [map_sub, hFix x]
  have hKi : IsCompactOperator ((U.comp T - (1 : E →L[𝕜] E)).comp i) := by
    simpa only [ContinuousLinearMap.coe_comp] using hUT.comp_clm i
  have hVCompact : IsCompactOperator (V.comp S - (1 : H →L[𝕜] H)) := by
    rw [hError]
    simpa only [ContinuousLinearMap.coe_comp] using hKi.clm_comp r
  have hEmbedding : Topology.IsClosedEmbedding S :=
    ContinuousLinearMap.isClosedEmbedding_of_injective_compact_left_parametrix
      S V hInjective hVCompact
  have hFactor : S.comp r = T := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro x
    have hProjection : i (r x) = H.projection T.ker hNH.symm.isCompl x := rfl
    have hResidual : x - i (r x) ∈ T.ker := by
      rw [hProjection]
      exact Submodule.sub_projection_mem hNH.symm.isCompl x
    have hTResidual : T (x - i (r x)) = 0 := hResidual
    rw [map_sub] at hTResidual
    change T (i (r x)) = T x
    exact (sub_eq_zero.mp hTResidual).symm
  have hQuotient : Topology.IsQuotientMap r :=
    Submodule.isQuotientMap_projectionOntoL hNH.symm
  have hStrictComp : Topology.IsStrictMap (S.comp r) := by
    change Topology.IsStrictMap ((S : H → F) ∘ (r : E → H))
    exact hQuotient.isStrictMap_iff.mp hEmbedding.isEmbedding.isStrictMap
  have hStrict : Topology.IsStrictMap T := by
    simpa only [hFactor] using hStrictComp
  have hRanges : Set.range (T : E → F) = Set.range (S : H → F) :=
    (congrArg (fun f : E →L[𝕜] F => Set.range (f : E → F)) hFactor).symm.trans
      (hQuotient.surjective.range_comp (S : H → F))
  have hClosed : IsClosed (T.range : Set F) := by
    change IsClosed (Set.range (T : E → F))
    rw [hRanges]
    exact hEmbedding.isClosed_range
  let : IsClosed (T.range : Set F) := hClosed
  let q : F →L[𝕜] (F ⧸ T.range) := T.range.mkQL
  have hqT : q.comp T = (0 : E →L[𝕜] (F ⧸ T.range)) := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro x
    change T.range.mkQ (T x) = 0
    have hMember : T x ∈ (T.range.mkQ).ker := by
      rw [Submodule.ker_mkQ]
      exact LinearMap.mem_range_self T.toLinearMap x
    exact hMember
  have hqError : q.comp (T.comp U - (1 : F →L[𝕜] F)) = -q := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro x
    change q (T (U x) - x) = -q x
    have hZero : q (T (U x)) = 0 := DFunLike.congr_fun hqT (U x)
    rw [map_sub, hZero, zero_sub]
  have hqErrorCompact :
      IsCompactOperator (q.comp (T.comp U - (1 : F →L[𝕜] F))) := by
    simpa only [ContinuousLinearMap.coe_comp] using hTU.clm_comp q
  have hqCompact : IsCompactOperator q := by
    have hNegq : IsCompactOperator (-q : F →L[𝕜] (F ⧸ T.range)) :=
      hqError ▸ hqErrorCompact
    have hNegNeg := hNegq.neg
    change IsCompactOperator (fun x : F => -(-q x)) at hNegNeg
    simpa only [neg_neg] using hNegNeg
  have hqOpen : IsOpenMap q :=
    T.range.isOpenQuotientMap_mkQL.isOpenMap
  have hCoker : T.range.CoFG :=
    FiniteDimensional.of_isCompactOperator_of_isOpenMap q hqCompact hqOpen
  exact ⟨hStrict, hClosed, hFinite, hCoker, hComplement⟩

end

end ContinuousLinearMap.IsFredholm

module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.OrthogonalSum
public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Fredholm.Prod
public import MathlibExt.Analysis.Normed.Operator.Fredholm.Transport

/-!
# Strong Fredholm orthogonal block sums

The existing rectangular block diagonal is transported from the actual
Cartesian product of two strong Fredholm maps through the stock WithLp
continuous linear equivalences. All five strong fields are preserved.
No scalar/stage completeness, Hilbert structure or new norm is required.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OrthogonalSum

universe u𝕜 uH₀ uH₁ uK₀ uK₁

variable {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
variable {H₀ : Type uH₀} {H₁ : Type uH₁} {K₀ : Type uK₀} {K₁ : Type uK₁}
variable [NormedAddCommGroup H₀] [NormedSpace 𝕜 H₀]
variable [NormedAddCommGroup H₁] [NormedSpace 𝕜 H₁]
variable [NormedAddCommGroup K₀] [NormedSpace 𝕜 K₀]
variable [NormedAddCommGroup K₁] [NormedSpace 𝕜 K₁]

/-- The actual rectangular orthogonal block of two strong Fredholm maps is
strong Fredholm, without completeness or inner-product hypotheses. -/
theorem isFredholm_blockDiagonal
    (S : H₀ →L[𝕜] H₁) (T : K₀ →L[𝕜] K₁)
    (hS : S.IsFredholm) (hT : T.IsFredholm) :
    (blockDiagonal S T).IsFredholm := by
  let d : OrthogonalSum H₀ K₀ ≃L[𝕜] H₀ × K₀ :=
    WithLp.prodContinuousLinearEquiv 2 𝕜 H₀ K₀
  let c : OrthogonalSum H₁ K₁ ≃L[𝕜] H₁ × K₁ :=
    WithLp.prodContinuousLinearEquiv 2 𝕜 H₁ K₁
  have hOperator : blockDiagonal S T =
      c.symm.toContinuousLinearMap.comp ((S.prodMap T).comp d.toContinuousLinearMap) := by
    ext x
    rfl
  rw [hOperator]
  exact (hS.prodMap hT).transport d c

end OrthogonalSum
